1.1 On the supplied branch [A2], fix $q=(s,V,n)\in W$ and $x=\Psi(q)$ in the original-coordinate uniqueness neighborhood of the local inverse [F3]. By openness, for $\lambda$ in some open interval about $1$, both $\lambda q\in W$ and $\lambda x$ remain in that uniqueness neighborhood and in the common-law entropy cone. Its fixed unit conversion commutes with multiplication by $\lambda$. Thus [A2] gives $S_c(\lambda\mathcal U_c(q),\lambda V,\lambda n)=\lambda S_c(x)=\lambda s$. By uniqueness of the inverse [F3], $\mathcal U_c(\lambda q)=\lambda\mathcal U_c(q)$ throughout this interval. Consequently [A2] supplies [A1] locally, without a global inverse claim. [given, A2, F3, construct]

2.1 For the general conclusion assume [A1], which step 1.1 supplies when [A2] applies. Since $W$ is open, at each $q\in W$ shrink the homogeneity interval so that $\lambda q\in W$ throughout it. 3.1 Substitute the conjugate derivatives from [F3] into step 2.1 to obtain $\mathcal U_c=Ts-pV+\sum_j\mu_jn_j$. [F3, step 2.1, algebra]

The extra common-law bulk postulate supplies the constitutive identification absent from the general tagged family. The theorem also retains its general conditional implication for any independently stipulated same-tag local energy law. The batch-8 countermodel concerns the broader tagged premises and lies outside this added branch; it remains nonlogical context. Neither local entropy inversion nor the differential identities assert global invertibility, admissibility across phase boundaries, or universal extensivity for finite, surface-sensitive, long-range or gravitating systems.

fm.title: Finite-bath canonical error under a smooth shell-entropy model
fm.physical_scope: A finite subsystem weakly coupled additively to a bath whose dimensionless shell entropy is twice continuously differentiable with bounded curvature on the full exchanged-energy interval; this is a conditional model bound, not a universal finite-size estimate.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §1.3 (printed pp. 17–20)
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §§4.2 and 4.4 (printed pp. 192–198 and 205–208)

sections.Statement:
Let the subsystem have a finite nonempty state set $\Omega$ and internal energies $E_x$ in joules with $|E_x|\le L$. A bath has a dimensionless shell entropy $s_B(u)$, defined on an open interval containing $[u_0-L,u_0+L]$ in joules, with $s_B\in C^2$ and $|s_B''(u)|\le M$ there; the model adopts $\beta=s'_B(u_0)>0$ in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$ and $T=(k_{\mathrm B}\beta)^{-1}$. Assume weak additive coupling and microcanonical shell sampling induce subsystem weights $P_B(x)\propto e^{s_B(u_0-E_x)}$. Let $P_C(x)=e^{-\beta E_x}/Z$ be the corresponding canonical law. With $\delta=ML^2/2$ (dimensionless), the shell log-weight remainder obeys
$$|s_B(u_0-E_x)-s_B(u_0)+\beta E_x|\le\delta,$$
and the normalized laws satisfy
$$\sum_{x\in\Omega}|P_B(x)-P_C(x)|\le e^{2\delta}-1.$$
This is an $\ell^1$ probability-vector bound; it does not assert a universal error or a thermodynamic limit.
sections.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** The finite subsystem, the bath entropy and curvature bound, the adopted energy-additive shell model, and the two normalized laws.

[F1] [[def-td-finite-microstate-model]]: $\Omega$ is finite and nonempty and each $E_x$ is a fixed internal energy in joules.

[F2] [[post-td-canonical-sampling]]: the canonical comparison law has weights $e^{-\beta E_x}/Z$ when $Z>0$ is finite.

[F3] [[post-td-microcanonical-sampling]]: the microcanonical joint-shell model assigns the subsystem marginal induced by the bath shell weights when the weak-additive-coupling and shell hypotheses are imposed.

[L1] [[thm-tdmath-finite-bath-error-bound]] (current batch 11 draft): for finite energies $|E_x|\le L$, $s_B\in C^2$ on the stated interval, $|s_B''|\le M$, $\beta=s'_B(u_0)$, and normalized weights proportional to $e^{s_B(u_0-E_x)}$, the Taylor remainder is at most $\delta=ML^2/2$ and the canonical comparison law has $\ell^1$ error at most $e^{2\delta}-1$. [A1] $L,M\ge0$, $\beta>0$, the bath interval contains every $u_0-E_x$, and the physical energy unit is joules, so $\beta E_x$, $s_B$, and $\delta$ are dimensionless.
sections.Proof:
**Given:** The finite-system energies, the smooth bath shell-entropy model, and the weak-additive microcanonical marginal stipulated in the Statement.

1.1 With $|E_x|\le L$, every bath argument $u_0-E_x$ lies in the stated interval. 2.1 Applying [L1] to these matched inputs gives $|s_B(u_0-E_x)-s_B(u_0)+\beta E_x|\le\delta$ for each state and $\sum_x|P_B(x)-P_C(x)|\le e^{2\delta}-1$. The claim is conditional on the actual shell-weight rule and the draft mathematical supplier, not on bath size alone. [F2, F3, L1, step 1.1] ∎

fm.title: Finite canonical partition, energy, variance, entropy and free-energy identities
fm.physical_scope: Exact finite-sum predictions for the adopted canonical law on a fixed finite microstate list with fixed internal energies; the statistical free-energy value is not automatically identified with a macroscopic Legendre potential or an empirical thermodynamic measurement.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §§1.3.1–1.3.4 (printed pp. 18–26)
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §§4.4–4.6 (printed pp. 205–217)

sections.Statement:
Let $(\Omega,\epsilon)$ be a finite microstate model with energies $E_x=\epsilon(x)\,\mathrm J$ from [[def-td-finite-microstate-model]]. Let $T>0$, $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$, and $P_\beta(x)=e^{-\beta E_x}/Z(\beta)$ be the adopted preparation of [[post-td-canonical-sampling]]. With $\bar E_\beta=\sum_xP_\beta(x)E_x$, $\operatorname{Var}_\beta(E)=\sum_xP_\beta(x)(E_x-\bar E_\beta)^2$, and $S_\beta=-k_{\mathrm B}\sum_xP_\beta(x)\log P_\beta(x)$, the finite partition sum is positive and
$$-\partial_\beta\log Z=\bar E_\beta,\qquad \partial_\beta^2\log Z=\operatorname{Var}_\beta(E),\qquad S_\beta=k_{\mathrm B}(\log Z+\beta\bar E_\beta).$$
Consequently the statistical free-energy value $F_{\mathrm{stat}}:=-k_{\mathrm B}T\log Z$ satisfies $F_{\mathrm{stat}}=\bar E_\beta-TS_\beta$. The derivatives hold the finite state set and its energy list fixed. No equivalence with a macroscopic entropy or Helmholtz potential is asserted.
sections.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** A finite nonempty state set, a fixed energy list in joules, $T>0$, the fixed SI value of $k_{\mathrm B}$, and the adopted canonical weights.

[F1] [[def-td-finite-microstate-model]]: $\Omega$ is finite and nonempty and each $E_x$ is a fixed energy in joules.

[F2] [[post-td-canonical-sampling]]: $P_\beta(x)=e^{-\beta E_x}/Z$ with $Z=\sum_xe^{-\beta E_x}$ and $\beta=1/(k_{\mathrm B}T)>0$ in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$.

[F3] [[thm-derivative-of-exponential]]: $\frac{d}{d\beta}e^{-\beta E_x}=-E_xe^{-\beta E_x}$ for each fixed $E_x$.

[F4] [[thm-logarithm-derivative-and-integral]] and [[def-natural-logarithm]]: for differentiable positive $Z$, $(\log Z)'=Z'/Z$.
sections.Proof:
**Given:** The finite canonical model and its fixed energy values.

1.1 Since $\Omega$ is finite and nonempty and every $e^{-\beta E_x}>0$, the finite sum $Z=\sum_xe^{-\beta E_x}$ is strictly positive and finite. The weights $P_\beta(x)$ therefore sum to one by their definition. [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 Differentiating the finite sum term by term using [F3] gives $Z'=-\sum_xE_xe^{-\beta E_x}$ and $Z''=\sum_xE_x^2e^{-\beta E_x}$. Applying [F4] yields $-\partial_\beta\log Z=-(Z'/Z)=\bar E_\beta$ and $\partial_\beta^2\log Z=Z''/Z-(Z'/Z)^2=\sum_xP_\beta(x)E_x^2-\bar E_\beta^2=\operatorname{Var}_\beta(E)$. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.1]

3.1 For each $x$, $\log P_\beta(x)=-\beta E_x-\log Z$. Substituting this into the finite entropy sum gives $S_\beta=-k_{\mathrm B}\sum_xP_\beta(x)\log P_\beta(x)=k_{\mathrm B}(\beta\bar E_\beta+\log Z)$. Since $\beta k_{\mathrm B}=1/T$, rearrangement gives $\bar E_\beta-TS_\beta=-k_{\mathrm B}T\log Z=F_{\mathrm{stat}}$. [F2, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

fm.title: Crooks path and work-distribution relation for a finite protocol
fm.physical_scope: A path-reversal identity for a finite-state protocol whose stage kernels are reversible with respect to their positive canonical laws; it does not extend to arbitrary driven systems without matching support and reversal assumptions.

references.title: C. Crooks, Entropy production fluctuation theorem and the nonequilibrium work relation for free energy differences
references.locator: Complete six-page paper; microscopic reversibility and canonical endpoint work relation.

references.title: U. Seifert, Stochastic thermodynamics, fluctuation theorems, and molecular machines
references.locator: Sections 3.2.3 and 4.4.1 on forward/reverse work distributions and reversed dynamics.

references.title: C. Jarzynski, Introduction to Nonequilibrium Statistical Physics, lecture notes, Nonequilibrium Work Relations
references.locator: Complete 21-page lecture PDF; comparison of forward and reverse work densities.

sections.Statement: Assume the setup of [[def-td-driven-finite-path-model]], the canonical initial law of [[post-td-canonical-protocol-preparation]], the stationarity model of [[post-td-stationary-bath-kernel]], and, additionally, $\pi_k(i)K_k(i,j)=\pi_k(j)K_k(j,i)$ for every $k,i,j$. For every forward path with positive probability, define its reverse probability by $P_R(\omega^R)=\pi_m(i_m)\prod_{k=1}^mK_k(i_k,i_{k-1})$. Then $P_R(\omega^R)>0$ and $P_F(\omega)/P_R(\omega^R)=e^{\beta(W(\omega)-\Delta F)}$. Consequently, at each work value $w$, $P_F(W=w)=e^{\beta(w-\Delta F)}P_R(W_R=-w)$. The reverse protocol first applies the stage-$k$ reverse transition at fixed $E_k$, then reverses the quench $E_k\to E_{k-1}$; its work is $W_R(\omega^R)=-W(\omega)$.
sections.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** The finite protocol with canonical initial and terminal laws, strictly positive $\pi_k$, stationary stage kernels, and the additional stagewise detailed-balance equations.

[F1] [[def-td-driven-finite-path-model]]: quench $k$ changes $E_{k-1}$ to $E_k$ before transition $K_k$; $W$ is work on the system.

[F2] [[def-td-detailed-balance-rate-model]]: the kernel balance equation is $\pi_k(i)K_k(i,j)=\pi_k(j)K_k(j,i)$.

[A1] [[post-td-canonical-protocol-preparation]]: the forward initial law is $\pi_0$.

[A2] [[post-td-stationary-bath-kernel]]: each $K_k$ preserves $\pi_k$.

[F3] [[pthm-td-finite-pathwise-first-law]]: $\Delta E=W+Q_{\mathrm{in}}$ with the stated signs.
sections.Proof:
**Given:** [F1], [F2], [A1], [A2], and [F3].

1.1 Define the reverse path law by starting with $\pi_m(i_m)$ and, in reverse order, using $K_k(i_k,i_{k-1})$ at fixed energy $E_k$ before undoing that quench. By detailed balance, if $K_k(i_{k-1},i_k)>0$ then $K_k(i_k,i_{k-1})>0$, because $\pi_k$ is strictly positive. Thus positive forward paths pair with positive reverse paths. [F1, F2, A1, A2]

2.1 On a paired path, divide the endpoint Gibbs weights and use detailed balance for each transition: $P_F(\omega)/P_R(\omega^R)=[\pi_0(i_0)/\pi_m(i_m)]\prod_{k=1}^m[\pi_k(i_k)/\pi_k(i_{k-1})]$. Substituting $\pi_k(i)=e^{-\beta E_k(i)}/Z_k$ and collecting terms gives $\log(P_F/P_R)=\beta[E_m(i_m)-E_0(i_0)-Q_{\mathrm{in}}]+\log(Z_m/Z_0)=\beta(W-\Delta F)$ by [F3]. [F1, F2, F3, A1, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 The reversed quench at stage $k$ occurs at state $i_{k-1}$, so its work term is $E_{k-1}(i_{k-1})-E_k(i_{k-1})=-[E_k(i_{k-1})-E_{k-1}(i_{k-1})]$; summing proves $W_R(\omega^R)=-W(\omega)$. Summing the path ratio over the finite set of paths with $W=w$ proves the stated distribution identity. [F1, F3, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume the setup of [[def-td-driven-finite-path-model]], the canonical initial law of [[post-td-canonical-protocol-preparation]], the stationarity model of [[post-td-stationary-bath-kernel]], and, additionally, $\pi_k(i)K_k(i,j)=\pi_k(j)K_k(j,i)$ for every $k,i,j$. For every forward path with positive probability, define its reverse probability by $P_R(\omega^R)=\pi_m(i_m)\prod_{k=1}^mK_k(i_k,i_{k-1})$. Then $P_R(\omega^R)>0$ and $P_F(\omega)/P_R(\omega^R)=e^{\beta(W(\omega)-\Delta F)}$. Consequently, at each work value $w$, $P_F(W=w)=e^{\beta(w-\Delta F)}P_R(W_R=-w)$. The reverse protocol first applies the stage-$k$ reverse transition at fixed $E_k$, then reverses the quench $E_k\to E_{k-1}$; its work is $W_R(\omega^R)=-W(\omega)$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The finite protocol with canonical initial and terminal laws, strictly positive $\pi_k$, stationary stage kernels, and the additional stagewise detailed-balance equations.

[F1] [[def-td-driven-finite-path-model]]: quench $k$ changes $E_{k-1}$ to $E_k$ before transition $K_k$; $W$ is work on the system.

[F2] [[def-td-detailed-balance-rate-model]]: the kernel balance equation is $\pi_k(i)K_k(i,j)=\pi_k(j)K_k(j,i)$.

[A1] [[post-td-canonical-protocol-preparation]]: the forward initial law is $\pi_0$.

[A2] [[post-td-stationary-bath-kernel]]: each $K_k$ preserves $\pi_k$.

[F3] [[pthm-td-finite-pathwise-first-law]]: $\Delta E=W+Q_{\mathrm{in}}$ with the stated signs.

## Proof

**Given:** [F1], [F2], [A1], [A2], and [F3].

1.1 Define the reverse path law by starting with $\pi_m(i_m)$ and, in reverse order, using $K_k(i_k,i_{k-1})$ at fixed energy $E_k$ before undoing that quench. By detailed balance, if $K_k(i_{k-1},i_k)>0$ then $K_k(i_k,i_{k-1})>0$, because $\pi_k$ is strictly positive. Thus positive forward paths pair with positive reverse paths. [F1, F2, A1, A2]

2.1 On a paired path, divide the endpoint Gibbs weights and use detailed balance for each transition: $P_F(\omega)/P_R(\omega^R)=[\pi_0(i_0)/\pi_m(i_m)]\prod_{k=1}^m[\pi_k(i_k)/\pi_k(i_{k-1})]$. Substituting $\pi_k(i)=e^{-\beta E_k(i)}/Z_k$ and collecting terms gives $\log(P_F/P_R)=\beta[E_m(i_m)-E_0(i_0)-Q_{\mathrm{in}}]+\log(Z_m/Z_0)=\beta(W-\Delta F)$ by [F3]. [F1, F2, F3, A1, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 The reversed quench at stage $k$ occurs at state $i_{k-1}$, so its work term is $E_{k-1}(i_{k-1})-E_k(i_{k-1})=-[E_k(i_{k-1})-E_{k-1}(i_{k-1})]$; summing proves $W_R(\omega^R)=-W(\omega)$. Summing the path ratio over the finite set of paths with $W=w$ proves the stated distribution identity. [F1, F3, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

[F4] [[thm-logarithm-derivative-and-integral]] and [[def-natural-logarithm]]: $\log t=\int_1^tdu/u$ for $t>0$.

[A1] The competitor has $r_x\ge0$, $\sum_xr_x=1$, and $\sum_xr_xE_x=\bar E$.
sections.Proof:
**Given:** The finite model, its canonical weights, and a competing probability vector with the same mean.

1.1 For every $t>0$, [F4] gives $\log t\le t-1$, with equality only at $t=1$: for $t>1$, integrate $1/u<1$ on $(1,t)$; for $0<t<1$, integrate $1/u>1$ on $(t,1)$ and reverse the endpoints. [A1] [[post-td-canonical-protocol-preparation]]: the initial law is $\pi_0(i)=e^{-\beta E_0(i)}/Z_0$.

[A2] [[post-td-stationary-bath-kernel]]: $\sum_i\pi_k(i)K_k(i,j)=\pi_k(j)$.

[L1] [[post-td-canonical-sampling]]: the current draft postulate adopts the finite microstate law $P_\beta(i)=e^{-\beta E(i)}/Z(\beta)$ for finite nonempty $\Omega$ with $0<Z(\beta)<\infty$ and $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$. sections.Proof:
**Proof technique:** induction on protocol stages.

**Given:** [F1], [A1], [A2], [L1], with the finite partition sums and canonical laws of the protocol.

1.1 For $k\ge1$ and $j\in\Omega$, define $S_k(j)$ by the finite sum over $i_0,\ldots,i_{k-1}\in\Omega$ of $\pi_0(i_0)\prod_{\ell=1}^kK_\ell(i_{\ell-1},i_\ell)e^{-\beta W_k}$, with $i_k=j$ and $W_k=\sum_{\ell=1}^k[E_\ell(i_{\ell-1})-E_{\ell-1}(i_{\ell-1})]$; put $S_0(j)=\pi_0(j)$. The canonical preparation gives the base $S_0(j)=\pi_0(j)=(Z_0/Z_0)\pi_0(j)$ by [A1] and the finite branch of [L1]. [F1, A1, L1, given, base, algebra]

2.1 For the induction step fix $k\in\{1,\ldots,m\}$ and suppose $S_{k-1}(i)=(Z_{k-1}/Z_0)\pi_{k-1}(i)$ for every $i$. [ih, step 1.1, F1]

3.1 Substitute this hypothesis in the recurrence from step 1.1. Since $\pi_{k-1}(i)=e^{-\beta E_{k-1}(i)}/Z_{k-1}$, the previous-stage Boltzmann factor cancels against the quench factor, giving $S_k(j)=(Z_k/Z_0)\sum_i\pi_k(i)K_k(i,j)=(Z_k/Z_0)\pi_k(j)$ by [A2]. 4.1 The base and induction step establish $S_k(j)=(Z_k/Z_0)\pi_k(j)$ for all stages. fm.title: Finite bosonic and fermionic mode partition and occupation formulas
fm.physical_scope: Declared finite lists of independent bosonic one-mode Fock systems or fermionic two-level occupation systems at assigned positive temperature; no interacting, infinite-mode, continuum, condensation, measured-occupation, or thermalization conclusion is asserted.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §§3.5–3.6 (printed pp. 77–106)
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §§5.6–5.7 (printed pp. 277–303)

sections.Statement:
Adopt the quantum Gibbs preparation of [[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] for a finite list of independent modes at $T>0$. For a bosonic mode with excitation energy $\varepsilon>0$ joules, let $q=e^{-\beta\varepsilon}$, $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$, and let $N$ be its dimensionless occupation number. Its partition trace and mean occupation are
$$Z_B=(1-q)^{-1},\qquad \langle N\rangle_B=\frac{q}{1-q}=\frac1{e^{\beta\varepsilon}-1}.$$
For a fermionic two-level occupation system with energies $0,\varepsilon$, the partition sum and excited-state occupation are
$$Z_F=1+q,\qquad \langle N\rangle_F=\frac{q}{1+q}=\frac1{e^{\beta\varepsilon}+1}.$$
For a finite independent collection, the corresponding partition traces multiply and each mode's marginal mean is the displayed one. These are exact model identities under the adopted preparation.
sections.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** The finite independent mode models, positive mode energies, assigned $T>0$, and the adopted Gibbs preparation.

[F1] [[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]]: the declared mode model is assigned $\rho_\beta=e^{-\beta G}/Z$ only under its stated self-adjoint-generator and finite-positive-trace conditions; this postulate assumes AC and Countable Choice.

[F2] [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-single-mode-thermal-trace]] (current carrier status says published): for $\omega>0$ and $\beta>0$, the one-mode bosonic trace is $(1-e^{-\beta\omega})^{-1}$ and the number mean is $1/(e^{\beta\omega}-1)$. The full proof was inspected; its published carrier lacks the required audit marker, so this use remains escalated.

[F3] [[lem-nrqm-many-body-two-level-thermal-formulas]] (current carrier status says published): for energies $0,\varepsilon$ with $\varepsilon,\beta>0$, $Z=1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}$ and the upper-level probability is $1/(e^{\beta\varepsilon}+1)$. Its full proof was inspected; the published carrier lacks the required audit marker, so this use remains escalated.

[F4] [[pthm-nrqm-many-body-thermal-occupation-predictions]] (current carrier status says published): the single-mode occupation readings are the stated Bose and Fermi means, under the postulate and assigned observable rules. Its full proof was inspected; the published carrier lacks the required audit marker, so this use remains escalated.

[F5] [[pthm-td-independent-factorization]]: for an explicitly independent finite product model, partition functions factor and the product canonical law has the subsystem marginals.

[F6] [[def-td-si-quantities]] and [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]: $\varepsilon$ is in joules, $T$ in kelvins, $\beta$ in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, and the occupation number is dimensionless.

[A1] Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice are assumed because the cited one-mode and mode-occupation supplier statements explicitly assume them.
sections.Proof:
**Given:** The mode energies, the independent finite mode list, $T>0$, and the quantum canonical preparation.

1.1 For one bosonic mode, [F2] gives $Z_B=(1-q)^{-1}$ and $\langle N\rangle_B=q/(1-q)$; for $q=e^{-\beta\varepsilon}$, multiplication of numerator and denominator by $e^{\beta\varepsilon}$ gives $q/(1-q)=1/(e^{\beta\varepsilon}-1)$. The unit convention in [F6] makes the exponent dimensionless. [F1, F2, F4, F6, A1, algebra]

1.2 For one fermionic occupation, [F3] gives $Z_F=1+q$ and upper-level probability $q/(1+q)$; multiplying numerator and denominator by $e^{\beta\varepsilon}$ gives $q/(1+q)=1/(e^{\beta\varepsilon}+1)$. [F1, F3, F4, F6, A1, algebra]

2.1 For a finite independent collection, apply [F5] repeatedly to factor the full partition trace into the product of its one-mode factors. Summing the product law over all other mode labels leaves each single-mode marginal unchanged, so the means in steps 1.1–1.2 apply componentwise. [F5, step 1.1, step 1.2] ∎

## Statement

Adopt the quantum Gibbs preparation of [[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] for a finite list of independent modes at $T>0$. For a bosonic mode with excitation energy $\varepsilon>0$ joules, let $q=e^{-\beta\varepsilon}$, $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$, and let $N$ be its dimensionless occupation number. Its partition trace and mean occupation are
$$Z_B=(1-q)^{-1},\qquad \langle N\rangle_B=\frac{q}{1-q}=\frac1{e^{\beta\varepsilon}-1}.$$
For a fermionic two-level occupation system with energies $0,\varepsilon$, the partition sum and excited-state occupation are
$$Z_F=1+q,\qquad \langle N\rangle_F=\frac{q}{1+q}=\frac1{e^{\beta\varepsilon}+1}.$$
For a finite independent collection, the corresponding partition traces multiply and each mode's marginal mean is the displayed one. These are exact model identities under the adopted preparation.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The finite independent mode models, positive mode energies, assigned $T>0$, and the adopted Gibbs preparation.

[F1] [[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]]: the declared mode model is assigned $\rho_\beta=e^{-\beta G}/Z$ only under its stated self-adjoint-generator and finite-positive-trace conditions; this postulate assumes AC and Countable Choice.

[F2] [[thm-nrqm-fock-and-equilibrium-single-mode-thermal-trace]] (current carrier status says published): for $\omega>0$ and $\beta>0$, the one-mode bosonic trace is $(1-e^{-\beta\omega})^{-1}$ and the number mean is $1/(e^{\beta\omega}-1)$. The full proof was inspected; its published carrier lacks the required audit marker, so this use remains escalated.

[F3] [[lem-nrqm-many-body-two-level-thermal-formulas]] (current carrier status says published): for energies $0,\varepsilon$ with $\varepsilon,\beta>0$, $Z=1+e^{-\beta\varepsilon}$ and the upper-level probability is $1/(e^{\beta\varepsilon}+1)$. Its full proof was inspected; the published carrier lacks the required audit marker, so this use remains escalated.

[F4] [[pthm-nrqm-many-body-thermal-occupation-predictions]] (current carrier status says published): the single-mode occupation readings are the stated Bose and Fermi means, under the postulate and assigned observable rules. Its full proof was inspected; the published carrier lacks the required audit marker, so this use remains escalated.

[F5] [[pthm-td-independent-factorization]]: for an explicitly independent finite product model, partition functions factor and the product canonical law has the subsystem marginals.

[F6] [[def-td-si-quantities]] and [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]: $\varepsilon$ is in joules, $T$ in kelvins, $\beta$ in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, and the occupation number is dimensionless.

[A1] Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice are assumed because the cited one-mode and mode-occupation supplier statements explicitly assume them.

## Proof

**Given:** The mode energies, the independent finite mode list, $T>0$, and the quantum canonical preparation.

1.1 For one bosonic mode, [F2] gives $Z_B=(1-q)^{-1}$ and $\langle N\rangle_B=q/(1-q)$; for $q=e^{-\beta\varepsilon}$, multiplication of numerator and denominator by $e^{\beta\varepsilon}$ gives $q/(1-q)=1/(e^{\beta\varepsilon}-1)$. The unit convention in [F6] makes the exponent dimensionless. [F1, F2, F4, F6, A1, algebra]

1.2 For one fermionic occupation, [F3] gives $Z_F=1+q$ and upper-level probability $q/(1+q)$; multiplying numerator and denominator by $e^{\beta\varepsilon}$ gives $q/(1+q)=1/(e^{\beta\varepsilon}+1)$. [F1, F3, F4, F6, A1, algebra]

2.1 For a finite independent collection, apply [F5] repeatedly to factor the full partition trace into the product of its one-mode factors. Summing the product law over all other mode labels leaves each single-mode marginal unchanged, so the means in steps 1.1–1.2 apply componentwise. [F5, step 1.1, step 1.2] ∎

sections.Statement:
Work in the nonzero finite-dimensional fixed-$N$ sector of [[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]], with self-adjoint energy $H_N^\sigma$ in joules and assigned $T>0$ in kelvins. Adopt the Gibbs preparation of [[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] and its unit convention $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$. For $F(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)-T S(\rho)$ over the declared sector density operators, the canonical preparation is the unique minimizer and
$$\min_\rho F(\rho)=F_{\mathrm{eq}}=-k_{\mathrm B}T\log\operatorname{tr}(e^{-\beta H_N^\sigma}).$$
This quantum statistical functional is not identified here with a macroscopic Helmholtz potential without an additional model bridge; its minimum does not establish equilibration.
sections.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** A nonzero finite-dimensional fixed-$N$ sector, its self-adjoint energy, an assigned $T>0$, and the adopted canonical preparation.

[F1] [[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]]: on the finite-dimensional sector, $S(\rho)=k_{\mathrm B}s(\rho)$ and $F(\rho)=\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)-k_{\mathrm B}T s(\rho)$, with $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$.

[F2] [[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]] and [[pthm-nrqm-many-body-thermal-equilibrium-characterization]] (both current carrier statuses say published): the former adopts the finite-sector Gibbs preparation under its exact AC/Countable Choice and finite positive-trace hypotheses; the latter proves that this preparation uniquely minimizes the declared finite-sector functional with minimum $-k_{\mathrm B}T\log Z_N$. Their current statements and the theorem proof were inspected, but their published records lack the required audit/source-review evidence, so this use remains escalated.

[F3] [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] and [[def-td-si-quantities]]: $H_N^\sigma$ and $F$ are in joules, $T$ in kelvins, and $k_{\mathrm B}$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$.

[A1] The Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice are assumed as required by [F2]; the sector dimension is finite and at least one.
sections.Proof:
**Given:** The declared finite-sector quantum model, the entropy/free-energy functional, and the canonical Gibbs assignment.

1.1 The finite-sector class, assigned positive temperature, canonical preparation, and entropy functional in the Statement are exactly the hypotheses and definitions of [F1]–[F2]. Countable Choice is stated explicitly in [A1], as required by [F2]. [F1, F2, F3, A1]

2.1 By [F2], every declared sector preparation obeys $F(\rho)\ge-k_{\mathrm B}T\log Z_N$, with equality only for the canonical preparation. Replacing $\beta^{-1}$ by $k_{\mathrm B}T$ using [F1]–[F3] gives the displayed minimum and units. This is a conditional preparation-model deduction, not a claim that dynamics reaches the minimizer. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1] ∎

fm.title: Fixed-temperature and fixed-pressure potential minimum with internal reactions
fm.physical_scope: A closed reacting system at fixed positive reservoir temperature and fixed external pressure, with internal stoichiometric changes and the exact ideal-reservoir/store model stated here; no external matter exchange, omitted work channel, nonideal reservoir, or kinetic relaxation claim is included.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, author-hosted complete lecture notes, §§4.3–4.4

sections.Statement:
Fix a system at a positive temperature $T_0$ and external pressure $p_0>0$. Internal reaction extents may vary in a declared feasible set, but no species crosses the system's outer boundary. The system contacts only an ideal thermal reservoir at $T_0$ and an ideal pressure store at $p_0$; all other work coordinates and excluded-energy changes are absent. Let $U$ be system internal energy in joules, $V$ volume in $\mathrm{m^3}$, and $S$ system entropy in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. Define the constrained potential
$$
\Phi_{T_0,p_0}:=U+p_0V-T_0S.
$$
For every admitted spontaneous endpoint change, $\Delta\Phi_{T_0,p_0}\le0$. If the system-plus-reservoir-plus-store endpoint is an attained global entropy maximum on its exact feasible set, then the corresponding system endpoint attains a global minimum of $\Phi_{T_0,p_0}$ over the induced feasible reaction states. This is a conditional model deduction; it does not assert that arbitrary fixed-$T,p$ reactions have this preparation or that the system reaches the minimum dynamically.
sections.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** A closed system with fixed outer boundary, internal reaction extents in an explicitly declared feasible set, an ideal bath and pressure store, an isolated compound containing the system and both auxiliaries, and an attained global entropy-maximizing endpoint. Amount changes are internal; the auxiliaries exchange neither matter nor any unlisted work channel.

[A1] Ideal thermal bath: for $T_0>0$, its entropy is $S_R(E_R)=S_{R,0}+E_R/T_0$ on the admitted reservoir energy interval. If heat $Q$ enters the system, $\Delta E_R=-Q$, so $\Delta S_R=-Q/T_0$.

[A2] Ideal pressure store: its energy changes by $p_0\Delta V$ when the system volume changes by $\Delta V$, and its entropy is constant. The only system work is $W_{\rm on}=-p_0\Delta V$. Thus the fixed-total-energy constraint is $\Delta U+\Delta E_R+p_0\Delta V=0$.

[A3] The system, bath, and pressure store form the isolated compound in the adopted macroscopic second-law and stable-equilibrium model. No matter crosses the compound's outer boundary; internal stoichiometric changes do not alter the ideal bath formulas.

[F1] [[post-td-first-law-energy]]: For an admitted closed process with no excluded-energy endpoint change, $\Delta U=Q+W_{\rm on}$.

[F2] [[post-td-macroscopic-second-law]]: The total endpoint entropy of the admitted isolated compound does not decrease.

[F3] [[post-td-entropy-maximum]]: Stable equilibrium is an attained global maximum of total entropy on the exact feasible endpoint set.

[F4] [[def-td-si-quantities]]: $U,Q,W_{\rm on}$ and $p_0V$ are in joules; $T_0$ is in kelvins; $S$ is in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, so $\Phi_{T_0,p_0}$ is in joules.
sections.Proof:
1.1 By [A2] and [F1], $\Delta U=Q-p_0\Delta V$. By [A1], $\Delta S_{\rm tot}=\Delta S-Q/T_0$, where $\Delta S$ is the system entropy change. Therefore
$$
\Delta\Phi_{T_0,p_0} =\Delta U+p_0\Delta V-T_0\Delta S =Q-T_0\Delta S =-T_0\Delta S_{\rm tot}\le0
$$
by $T_0>0$ and [F2]. The derivation does not depend on whether $\Delta n_j$ arises from an internal reaction. [given, A1, A2, F1, F2, F4, algebra]

2.1 On the exact fixed-total-energy feasible set, [A1]–[A2] give $E_R=E_{\rm tot}-U-p_0V$ up to a fixed reference constant. Hence
$$
S_{\rm tot}=S+S_R =\mathrm{constant}+S-\frac{U+p_0V}{T_0} =\mathrm{constant}-\frac{\Phi_{T_0,p_0}}{T_0}.
$$
Since $T_0>0$, an attained global maximizer of $S_{\rm tot}$ is exactly a global minimizer of $\Phi_{T_0,p_0}$ on the induced feasible reaction states, by [F3]. [given, A1, A2, A3, F3, algebra] ∎
sections.Remarks: The argument is the fixed-reservoir entropy bookkeeping extended to internal changes of species amounts. It does not cover an open matter reservoir, which would contribute chemical-potential terms, or an external work channel not included in [A2].

\Delta\Phi_{T_0,p_0} =\Delta U+p_0\Delta V-T_0\Delta S =Q-T_0\Delta S =-T_0\Delta S_{\rm tot}\le0
$$
by $T_0>0$ and [F2]. The derivation does not depend on whether $\Delta n_j$ arises from an internal reaction. [given, A1, A2, F1, F2, F4, algebra]

2.1 On the exact fixed-total-energy feasible set, [A1]–[A2] give $E_R=E_{\rm tot}-U-p_0V$ up to a fixed reference constant. Hence
$$
S_{\rm tot}=S+S_R =\mathrm{constant}+S-\frac{U+p_0V}{T_0} =\mathrm{constant}-\frac{\Phi_{T_0,p_0}}{T_0}.
$$
Since $T_0>0$, an attained global maximizer of $S_{\rm tot}$ is exactly a global minimizer of $\Phi_{T_0,p_0}$ on the induced feasible reaction states, by [F3]. [given, A1, A2, A3, F3, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

The argument is the fixed-reservoir entropy bookkeeping extended to internal changes of species amounts. It does not cover an open matter reservoir, which would contribute chemical-potential terms, or an external work channel not included in [A2].

## Statement

Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open time interval, $\Omega=\prod_{i=1}^3(0,L_i)$ a fixed rectangle, and $(T,u,j_Q,K)$ a field record from [[def-td-rectangular-local-equilibrium-fields]] satisfying the adopted local-energy, Fourier, and local-entropy postulates [[post-td-local-energy-balance]], [[post-td-fourier-conductivity]], and [[post-td-local-equilibrium-entropy-density]]. ## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A rectangular field record on $\overline\Omega\times I$ with $T>0$, $u=u(T)$, $c(T)=u'(T)>0$, $j_Q=-K(x,T)\nabla T$, $K_s\succeq0$, $\partial_tu+\operatorname{div}j_Q=0$, and $j_Q\cdot n=0$ on every face.

[F1] [[def-td-rectangular-local-equilibrium-fields]]: $T$ is $C^1$ in time and $C^2$ in space up to the rectangular faces; $u$ and its heat capacity $c=u'$ are the stated local functions, and $\nabla$ and $\operatorname{div}$ are Euclidean coordinate derivatives.

[A2] [[post-td-fourier-conductivity]]: $j_Q=-K\nabla T$ and $z^{\mathsf T}K_s z\ge0$ for every $z\in\mathbb R^3$.

[A4] The flux $j_Q$ and its first spatial derivatives are continuous on each compact time slab through the boundary, so the coordinate divergence and face traces in the proof are defined and integrable.

[F2] [[thm-newton-leibniz-with-interior-derivative]]: a continuously differentiable coordinate function on a closed interval has its derivative integral equal to its endpoint increment.

[F3] [[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]]: iterated Riemann integrals of continuous functions on product rectangles equal the multidimensional integral.

1.2 Substituting $j_Q=-K\nabla T$ from [A2] makes the right side $(\nabla T)^{\mathsf T}K\nabla T/T^2$. [A2, F1, algebra]

1.3 For each coordinate $i$, apply [F2] to the $i$th component of $j_Q/T$ on $[0,L_i]$: its integral is the endpoint difference $[(j_Q)_i/T]_{x_i=0}^{x_i=L_i}$. By [F3] these one-dimensional integrals may be integrated over the other two coordinates and summed. The result is $\int_\Omega\operatorname{div}(j_Q/T)\,dx=0$ because $j_Q\cdot n=0$ on every face and $T>0$. The same calculation gives $\int_\Omega\operatorname{div}j_Q\,dx=0$. [F2, F3, A1, A4]

fm.title: General quantum Gibbs normalization and canonical identities
fm.physical_scope: A declared quantum model with a semibounded self-adjoint energy operator, trace-class Gibbs exponential, and local first-and-second-moment envelope; the result concerns the adopted Gibbs preparation and does not derive thermalization or a continuum spectrum.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §§1.3.1–1.3.4 (printed pp. 18–26)
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §§4.3–4.4 (printed pp. 199–208)

sections.Statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice and the canonical Gibbs-preparation assumption [[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]]. Restrict to its $G=H$ branch: the declared energy operator $H$ is self-adjoint, bounded below, and measured in joules; $T>0$ is in kelvins, $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ is in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, and $K_\beta=e^{-\beta H}$ has $0<Z_\beta=\operatorname{Tr}K_\beta<\infty$. Suppose also that on an open interval $J_\beta\subset(0,\infty)$ containing $\beta$, every compact $C\subset J_\beta$ admits a summable family $a_j\ge0$ with $(1+|E_j|^2)e^{-\gamma E_j}\le a_j$ for all energy eigenvalues $E_j$ and $\gamma\in C$. For the adopted density $\rho_\beta=K_\beta/Z_\beta$, the mean and variance of $H$ are finite and
$$-\partial_\beta\log Z_\beta=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_\beta H),\qquad \partial_\beta^2\log Z_\beta=\operatorname{Var}_{\rho_\beta}(H),\qquad S_{\mathrm{vN}}(\rho_\beta)=k_{\mathrm B}\bigl(\log Z_\beta+\beta\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_\beta H)\bigr).$$
Thus $F_{\mathrm{stat}}=-k_{\mathrm B}T\log Z_\beta=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_\beta H)-T S_{\mathrm{vN}}(\rho_\beta)$. This statement does not extend the Helmholtz interpretation to an effective generator $H-\mu\mathcal N$.
sections.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** A nonzero quantum Hilbert space, a self-adjoint energy operator $H$ bounded below, a positive assigned temperature, the adopted Gibbs preparation, a finite positive trace, and the local summable moment envelope.

[F1] [[post-nrqm-many-body-canonical-equilibrium-ensemble]]: for a declared $G=H$ model with self-adjoint semibounded generator and $0<\operatorname{Tr}e^{-\beta H}<\infty$, the adopted preparation is $\rho_\beta=e^{-\beta H}/Z_\beta$; the postulate explicitly assumes AC and Countable Choice and does not assert equilibration.

[F2] [[def-nrqm-many-body-framework-entropy-and-free-energy]] and [[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]]: in the finite-sector class, $S=k_{\mathrm B}s$ and $\beta=1/(k_{\mathrm B}T)$; the general quantum model assigns energy and temperature units but does not by itself identify a trace functional with a macroscopic state function.

[L1] [[thm-tdmath-general-trace-gibbs-model]] (current batch 11 draft): for a semibounded self-adjoint operator with trace-class Gibbs exponential and the stated local moment envelope, the Gibbs weight has a countable energy eigenfamily and the normalized eigenvalue law satisfies the summable canonical mean, variance, and entropy identities. Its full current proof was inspected; its draft status remains conditional.

[F3] [[def-td-si-quantities]]: $k_{\mathrm B}$ is in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, $T$ in kelvins, and energy in joules; hence $\beta$ is in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$ and $\beta E_j$ is dimensionless.

[A1] The full Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice are assumed at the exact strengths required by [F1] and [L1].
sections.Proof:
**Given:** The $G=H$ reading of the adopted quantum Gibbs preparation, trace finiteness, and the local moment envelope.

1.1 By [F1], $K_\beta=e^{-\beta H}$ is the declared positive Gibbs weight and $\rho_\beta=K_\beta/Z_\beta$ is the model's adopted preparation. The semiboundedness, positive finite trace, AC assumptions and moment envelope in the Statement match the hypotheses of [L1]. [F1, F3, L1, A1]

2.1 Applying [L1] to this operator yields the finite mean and variance identities and the dimensionless spectral entropy identity $\frac{S_{\mathrm{vN}}}{k_{\mathrm B}}=\log Z_\beta+\beta\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_\beta H)$. Multiplying by $k_{\mathrm B}$ and using $\beta k_{\mathrm B}=1/T$ gives $F_{\mathrm{stat}}=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_\beta H)-T S_{\mathrm{vN}}=-k_{\mathrm B}T\log Z_\beta$. The deduction is conditional on [L1] and the adopted preparation; it asserts no dynamics. [F1, F2, F3, L1, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

fm.title: Heat-capacity relation on a stable response chart
fm.physical_scope: Whole-system heat capacities and response coefficients on a C2, positive-temperature, fixed-composition simple-compressible chart with a valid pressure-volume response inverse and positive isothermal compressibility; singular and critical charts are excluded.

references.title: Daniel Arovas, Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §2.10.5
Jeremy Tatum, Heat and Thermodynamics, §13.3, Pressure and Temperature

sections.Statement:
On an open C2 Helmholtz chart $F(T,V,n)$ at fixed composition $n$, suppose $T>0$, $V>0$, the response coordinates $(T,p,n)$ have the local inverse required by [[def-td-response-functions]], and $\kappa_T>0$. Then

$$C_p-C_V=\frac{TV\alpha_p^2}{\kappa_T}.$$

Here $C_V,C_p$ are the whole-system heat capacities, $\alpha_p=V^{-1}(\partial V/\partial T)_{p,n}$, and $\kappa_T=-V^{-1}(\partial V/\partial p)_{T,n}$, all as in [[def-td-response-functions]]. The formula is a conditional model identity, not an empirical law or a claim at singular response points.
sections.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** A fixed-composition open C2 chart with $T,V>0$, the valid local pressure response inverse, and finite derivatives in the Statement.

[F1] [[def-td-response-functions]]: $C_V=(\partial U/\partial T)_{V,n}$, $C_p=(\partial H/\partial T)_{p,n}$, $\kappa_T=-V^{-1}(\partial V/\partial p)_{T,n}$, and $\alpha_p=V^{-1}(\partial V/\partial T)_{p,n}$; the definitions assert no response identities.

[F2] [[pthm-td-potential-differentials]]: $dF=-s\,dT-p\,dV+\sum_j\mu_j\,dn_j$ and $dH=T\,ds+V\,dp+\sum_j\mu_j\,dn_j$ on valid charts.

[F3] [[pthm-td-maxwell-relations]]: $s_V|_{T,n}=p_T|_{V,n}$ on the Helmholtz chart.

[F4] [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]: Derivatives of compositions obey the total-derivative chain rule.

[F5] [[thm-chain-sum-product-and-composition-rules-for-banach-derivatives]]: The derivative of a product of differentiable scalar maps is the sum of the two product terms.
sections.Proof:
1.1 At fixed $V,n$, $U=F+Ts$ and $F_T=-s$ from [F2], so the product rule [F5] gives $C_V=U_T|_{V,n}=T s_T|_{V,n}$. At fixed $p,n$, $dH=T\,ds+V\,dp$ from [F2], hence $C_p=H_T|_{p,n}=T s_T|_{p,n}$. [given, F2, F5, algebra]

1.2 Differentiating $p(T,V(T,p,n),n)=p$ in $T$ at fixed $p,n$ gives $p_T|_{V,n}+p_V|_{T,n}V_T|_{p,n}=0$. The response inverse in the hypothesis makes these derivatives valid, and [F1] gives $p_V|_{T,n}=-1/(V\kappa_T)$. Thus $p_T|_{V,n}=\alpha_p/\kappa_T$. [given, F1, F4, algebra]

2.1 Along a constant-$p$, fixed-$n$ curve, [F4] gives $s_T|_{p,n}=s_T|_{V,n}+s_V|_{T,n}V_T|_{p,n}$. Subtract the two identities in step 1.1 and use [F3] to obtain $C_p-C_V=T p_T|_{V,n}V_T|_{p,n}$. [F1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

## Statement

On an open C2 Helmholtz chart $F(T,V,n)$ at fixed composition $n$, suppose $T>0$, $V>0$, the response coordinates $(T,p,n)$ have the local inverse required by [[def-td-response-functions]], and $\kappa_T>0$. Then

$$C_p-C_V=\frac{TV\alpha_p^2}{\kappa_T}.$$

Here $C_V,C_p$ are the whole-system heat capacities, $\alpha_p=V^{-1}(\partial V/\partial T)_{p,n}$, and $\kappa_T=-V^{-1}(\partial V/\partial p)_{T,n}$, all as in [[def-td-response-functions]]. The formula is a conditional model identity, not an empirical law or a claim at singular response points.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A fixed-composition open C2 chart with $T,V>0$, the valid local pressure response inverse, and finite derivatives in the Statement.

[F1] [[def-td-response-functions]]: $C_V=(\partial U/\partial T)_{V,n}$, $C_p=(\partial H/\partial T)_{p,n}$, $\kappa_T=-V^{-1}(\partial V/\partial p)_{T,n}$, and $\alpha_p=V^{-1}(\partial V/\partial T)_{p,n}$; the definitions assert no response identities.

[F2] [[pthm-td-potential-differentials]]: $dF=-s\,dT-p\,dV+\sum_j\mu_j\,dn_j$ and $dH=T\,ds+V\,dp+\sum_j\mu_j\,dn_j$ on valid charts.

[F3] [[pthm-td-maxwell-relations]]: $s_V|_{T,n}=p_T|_{V,n}$ on the Helmholtz chart.

1.2 Differentiating $p(T,V(T,p,n),n)=p$ in $T$ at fixed $p,n$ gives $p_T|_{V,n}+p_V|_{T,n}V_T|_{p,n}=0$. The response inverse in the hypothesis makes these derivatives valid, and [F1] gives $p_V|_{T,n}=-1/(V\kappa_T)$. Thus $p_T|_{V,n}=\alpha_p/\kappa_T$. [given, F1, F4, algebra]

fm.title: Partition, Gibbs-entropy and free-energy factorization for independent finite systems
fm.physical_scope: Finite composite models whose state set is explicitly the Cartesian product and whose microscopic energy is additive; no claim is made for interacting systems, interface terms, or experimental independence.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §1.3.1 (printed pp. 18–19)
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §§4.4.1 and 4.6 (printed pp. 205–217)

sections.Statement: Let two finite microstate models from [[def-td-finite-microstate-model]] have nonempty state sets $\Omega_A,\Omega_B$, energies $E_A,E_B$ in joules, and the same $T>0$. Assume their declared composite model has state set $\Omega_A\times\Omega_B$ and energy $E_{AB}(x,y)=E_A(x)+E_B(y)$, with no interaction term. Under the canonical sampling assumption [[post-td-canonical-sampling]], the partition function factorizes as $Z_{AB}=Z_AZ_B$, the joint canonical law is $P_{AB}=P_AP_B$, the Gibbs entropy satisfies $S_{AB}=S_A+S_B$, and the statistical free-energy value satisfies $F_{AB}=F_A+F_B$.
sections.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** Two finite nonempty state sets, additive composite energy, fixed $T>0$, and the canonical preparations of both subsystems and their composite.

[F1] [[def-td-finite-microstate-model]]: each state set is finite and nonempty and the composite state set and additive energy are declared model data.

[F2] [[post-td-canonical-sampling]]: for each model, $P(x)=e^{-\beta E(x)}/Z$ with $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$.

[F3] [[pthm-td-finite-canonical-identities]]: $S=-k_{\mathrm B}\sum_xP(x)\log P(x)$ and $F=\bar E-TS=-k_{\mathrm B}T\log Z$ for each finite model.
sections.Proof:
**Given:** The finite product state set, additive energy, and the three canonical laws.

1.1 For every $(x,y)\in\Omega_A\times\Omega_B$, $e^{-\beta E_{AB}(x,y)}=e^{-\beta E_A(x)}e^{-\beta E_B(y)}$. Reindexing the finite sum over the Cartesian product therefore gives $Z_{AB}=(\sum_xe^{-\beta E_A(x)})(\sum_ye^{-\beta E_B(y)})=Z_AZ_B$. Dividing the product weight by $Z_AZ_B$ gives $P_{AB}(x,y)=P_A(x)P_B(y)$. [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 Since each probability is positive, $\log P_{AB}(x,y)=\log P_A(x)+\log P_B(y)$. Summing against $P_A(x)P_B(y)$ and using the finite normalizations yields $S_{AB}=S_A+S_B$. The mean energy is $\bar E_{AB}=\bar E_A+\bar E_B$ by the same finite factorization, so $F_{AB}=\bar E_{AB}-TS_{AB}=F_A+F_B$. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

fm.title: Intensive equilibrium conditions for coexisting phases
fm.physical_scope: Finite coexisting phase branches in positive-temperature C2 charts at an attained global entropy maximum, and only the energy, volume, or species transfers declared pairwise feasible in both directions.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, author-hosted complete lecture notes, §5.1.1
Konstantin K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics: Statistical Mechanics, §4.1 First-order phase transitions

sections.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** A finite number of named phase branches, a positive-mole composition chart, an attained global entropy maximum on the exact feasible set, C2 entropy on each phase chart, finite positive temperatures, additive separated-system coordinates and entropy, and the bilateral local feasibility of each exchange direction used below. Use SI units.

[A1] [[post-td-entropy-maximum]]: A stable endpoint attains a global maximum of total entropy on its exact feasible endpoint set; local maxima alone are not called stable equilibrium.

[F1] [[def-td-phase-and-coexistence-domain]] and [[def-td-isolated-compound-feasible-set]]: Phase amounts and states lie in the declared branch charts and exact feasible set; only the listed totals and exchanges may vary.

[F2] [[post-td-bulk-additivity]] and [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]]: For the specified separated compound, energy, volume, aligned species amounts, and entropy add; on each selected single-phase chart the entropy is finite and C2 with $S_U>0$.

[F3] [[def-td-temperature-pressure-chemical-potential]]: $S_U=1/T$, $S_V=p/T$, and $S_{n_j}=-\mu_j/T$, each partial holding the other physical coordinates fixed.

[L1] [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]: The derivative of a differentiable composition is the composition of its derivatives.
sections.Proof:
1.1 Fix any pair $\alpha,\beta$ and an allowed energy transfer. For any fixed nonzero increment $h$ joules, bilateral local feasibility supplies the curve $U_\alpha(t)=U_\alpha^*+th$, $U_\beta(t)=U_\beta^*-th$ for all sufficiently small $t$ of either sign, with all other coordinates fixed. The total entropy along this curve has a local maximum at $t=0$ by [A1]. Its derivative exists by [F2]; the right difference quotients are nonpositive and the left difference quotients are nonnegative, so the derivative is zero. By additivity and [L1], this derivative is $h(S_{\alpha,U}-S_{\beta,U})$. Since $h\ne0$, $S_{\alpha,U}=S_{\beta,U}$. [given, A1, F1, F2, L1, construct]

2.1 By [F3], $S_{\alpha,U}=1/T_\alpha$ and $S_{\beta,U}=1/T_\beta$. Both temperatures are finite and positive, so equality of the reciprocals gives $T_\alpha=T_\beta$. [given, F3, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 If volume transfer is permitted, take a nonzero increment $k$ in $\mathrm{m^3}$ and vary $V_\alpha(t)=V_\alpha^*+tk$, $V_\beta(t)=V_\beta^*-tk$ with both signs feasible. The same local-maximum quotient argument gives $k(S_{\alpha,V}-S_{\beta,V})=0$, hence $S_{\alpha,V}=S_{\beta,V}$. By [F3], $p_\alpha/T_\alpha=p_\beta/T_\beta$. When energy transfer is also permitted, step 2.1 gives equal positive temperatures, so $p_\alpha=p_\beta$. These are derivative pressures; a mechanical piston interpretation requires its separately declared coupling. [given, A1, F1, F2, F3, L1, step 2.1, construct]

3.2 If species $j$ is transferable, vary its mole amounts by $n_{\alpha,j}(t)=n_{\alpha,j}^*+tq$ and $n_{\beta,j}(t)=n_{\beta,j}^*-tq$ for a nonzero increment $q$ in moles. Both signs are feasible. The same quotient argument gives $q(S_{\alpha,n_j}-S_{\beta,n_j})=0$, hence equal entropy partials. By [F3], $\mu_{\alpha,j}/T_\alpha=\mu_{\beta,j}/T_\beta$. If energy transfer is also permitted, step 2.1 gives equal positive temperatures and therefore equal chemical potentials. [given, A1, F1, F2, F3, L1, step 2.1, construct]

4.1 Every pair was arbitrary, so the asserted pairwise equalities hold for all named phases and only for the channels whose bilateral feasibility was assumed. If $P=1$, there are no pairs and the conditions are vacuous. No derivative equality follows for a retained or boundary coordinate because its required two-sided feasible curve is absent. [given, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 3.2] ∎

fm.title: Interacting exact-N shrinking-shell three-ensemble local limit
fm.physical_scope: Superstable regular classical positional Borel pair systems in periodic boxes, at positive temperature and interior density, with differentiable canonical rate and a singleton grand variational minimizer; local observables use the same periodic continuation, and kinetic momentum is excluded.

references.title: Hans-Otto Georgii, Large deviations and the equivalence of ensembles for Gibbsian particle systems with superstable interaction, Probability Theory and Related Fields 99 (1994), 171–195
David Tong, Statistical Physics (author-hosted Cambridge lecture notes)
Konstantin K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Part SM: Statistical Mechanics (2024 author-hosted lecture notes)

sections.Statement:
Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB as required by the current variational-pressure supplier. Let $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$, $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$, and assume $\widehat\varphi$ is Borel measurable. Require the exact superstable regular hypotheses of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]; use $\widehat H=H/E_0$ and $\widehat\beta=E_0\beta>0$ in its mathematical suppliers. Let $F(\rho,\beta)$ denote the numerical canonical rate evaluated at $\widehat\beta$; assume it is differentiable in physical $\beta$ at the chosen temperature and set $e=-\partial_\beta F(\rho,\beta)$, in joules per dimensionless reference volume. For periodic cubes $\Lambda_n$, take exact particle numbers $N_n$ with $N_n/V_n\to\rho$ at a positive interior attainable density. Choose a finite supporting activity parameter $\alpha$ for $F$ at $\rho$ and set $z=e^\alpha>0$; assume the corresponding stationary grand variational minimizer is the singleton $P^\ast$ as in [[post-td-grand-variational-phase-uniqueness]].

Then there exists a constructed sequence $\delta_n\downarrow0$ for which the periodic exact-$N_n$ canonical positional law, the periodic grand-canonical law at $(\alpha,\beta)$, and the uniform positional shell law of [[def-td-controlled-fixed-n-energy-shell]] on
$$N=N_n,\qquad |H_{N_n}^{\mathrm{per}}/V_n-e|\leq\delta_n$$
all converge locally to $P^\ast$. Convergence means convergence of expectations for every measurable local observable $f$ supported in a bounded region and satisfying $|f|\leq c(1+N_A)$ there. The shell sequence is constructed from canonical concentration; arbitrary preassigned shrinking widths, exact zero-width surfaces, full phase-space shells involving kinetic momentum, and a conclusion at nonunique minimizers are not asserted.

Here local observables are evaluated on the periodic continuation of the prepared torus configuration. This is the same periodic boundary preparation, with no new physical sampling assumption; a configuration is not extended by the empty configuration outside its fundamental cube.
sections.Facts & Assumptions:
[F1] [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]]: $H_N$ is positional pair energy in joules; no kinetic term is included.

fm.title: Invariance of a regular-shell microcanonical preparation
fm.physical_scope: A classical Hamiltonian flow that is globally defined and invertible on a compact regular energy band with the stated coarea measure; invariance is not ergodicity, mixing, equilibration, or equality of time and ensemble averages.

sections.Statement:
Let a physical Hamiltonian model satisfy [[def-td-regular-hamiltonian-shell-preparation]] on a nonempty compact regular energy band, and adopt its normalized shell law by [[post-td-microcanonical-sampling]]. In addition to the definition's $C^2$ regularity, assume its numerical Hamiltonian $\hat H$ is $C^\infty$ and its Hamiltonian flow $\phi_t$ is an invertible smooth map of the whole band for every $t\in\mathbb R$. Then, conditional on the current batch-12 draft mathematical interfaces [[thm-tdmath-hamiltonian-measure-and-recurrence]] and [[thm-tdmath-regular-energy-shell-measure]], every shell probability $
u_{\hat E}$ is invariant:
$$
u_{\hat E}(\phi_t^{-1}(A))=
u_{\hat E}(A)$$
for every Borel set $A\subseteq\Sigma_{\hat E}$ and every $t\in\mathbb R$. This result asserts no ergodicity, time-average equality, or thermalization.

**Given:** A canonical Hamiltonian chart, a nonempty compact regular energy shell, its normalized coarea preparation, and a globally defined invertible flow on the band.

[F1] [[def-td-regular-hamiltonian-shell-preparation]]: the dimensionless energy level is regular and compact and the normalized coarea probability $\nu_{\hat E}$ is defined.

[F2] [[post-td-microcanonical-sampling]]: on this admitted regular shell the assigned microcanonical preparation is $\nu_{\hat E}$.

[L1] [[thm-tdmath-hamiltonian-measure-and-recurrence]] (current batch 12 draft): under AC, a smooth Hamiltonian on a symplectic manifold has a local flow preserving symplectic volume wherever defined; completeness or global existence is not inferred. The current Statement and full proof are present and were inspected; Step 1 readiness is missing, so this premise remains conditionally used.

[L2] [[thm-tdmath-regular-energy-shell-measure]] (current batch 12 draft): for $C^2$ energy on an open Euclidean domain with compact regular energy bands, the coarea construction has finite positive mass on each nonempty shell; a Hamiltonian flow that is a diffeomorphism of a full compact band and preserves that band preserves each normalized shell measure. The current Statement and full proof are present and were inspected; Step 1 readiness is missing, so this premise remains conditionally used.

[A1] AC is included as the exact set-theoretic assumption of [L1]; no ergodicity hypothesis is assumed.

[A2] The numerical Hamiltonian is $C^\infty$, strengthening the shell definition's $C^2$ assumption to match [L1]; the flow is assumed to be a smooth invertible map of the whole band for every real $t$. This global-flow condition is not inferred from the local Hamiltonian equations.
sections.Proof:
**Given:** The regular-shell model, its adopted shell probability, AC, and an invertible smooth Hamiltonian flow defined on the full band.

1.1 By [F1] and [A2], the canonical Hamiltonian data, smoothness, and full-band invertible flow match the hypotheses of [L1]–[L2]. Energy is conserved along each flow line because $\frac{d}{dt}\hat H(\phi_t(x))=d\hat H(X_{\hat H})=\hat\omega(X_{\hat H},X_{\hat H})=0$; the global-flow condition is an assumption, not a consequence of local equations. [F1, L1, L2, A1, A2, given, algebra]

fm.title: Joule-Thomson coefficient on a valid Gibbs chart
fm.physical_scope: Local derivative identity for a closed-composition system on a positive-temperature C2 Gibbs response chart with nonzero constant-pressure heat capacity; it does not assert an open-flow throttle balance, a sign of cooling, or an empirical material coefficient.

references.title: Daniel Arovas, Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §2.10.6
Jeremy Tatum, Heat and Thermodynamics, §12.6, Joule and Joule-Thomson Coefficients

sections.Statement:
On a C2 Gibbs chart $G(T,p,n)$ at fixed composition $n$, with $T>0$, $V>0$, finite $C_p>0$, and a valid local inverse between $(T,p,n)$ and $(H,p,n)$, define the **Joule-Thomson coefficient** by

$$\mu_{JT}:=\left(\frac{\partial T}{\partial p}\right)_{H,n}.$$

Then

$$\mu_{JT}=\frac{T(\partial V/\partial T)_{p,n}-V}{C_p}=\frac{V(T\alpha_p-1)}{C_p},$$

where $\alpha_p=V^{-1}(\partial V/\partial T)_{p,n}$ and $C_p=(\partial H/\partial T)_{p,n}$ are the response functions of [[def-td-response-functions]]. This is a local derivative identity. It does not prove that a real throttle is isenthalpic or that a particular substance cools under expansion.
sections.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** A fixed-composition open C2 chart with valid $(T,p,n)$ and $(H,p,n)$ coordinates, $T,V,C_p>0$, and the potentials defined in [[def-td-legendre-potentials]].

[F1] [[pthm-td-potential-differentials]]: On a valid chart, $dH=T\,ds+V\,dp+\sum_j\mu_j\,dn_j$ and $dG=-s\,dT+V\,dp+\sum_j\mu_j\,dn_j$.

[F2] [[pthm-td-maxwell-relations]]: For the Gibbs chart, $s_p|_{T,n}=-V_T|_{p,n}$.

[F3] [[def-td-response-functions]]: $C_p=H_T|_{p,n}$ and $\alpha_p=V^{-1}V_T|_{p,n}$ on a valid response chart.

[F4] [[def-td-legendre-potentials]]: $H=U+pV$ and $G=H-Ts$ on their local natural-variable charts.

[F5] [[def-td-si-quantities]]: $p$ is in pascals, $V$ in cubic metres, $U,H,G$ in joules, and $T$ in kelvins, with $\mathrm{Pa\,m^3=J}$.
sections.Proof:
1.1 At fixed $n$, write $ds=s_T|_{p,n}\,dT+s_p|_{T,n}\,dp$ in [F1]. The enthalpy $H$ and chart are those of [F4]. Since $C_p=H_T|_{p,n}$ and $dH=T\,ds+V\,dp$, the coefficient of $dT$ gives $C_p=T s_T|_{p,n}$. Therefore $dH=C_p\,dT+(T s_p|_{T,n}+V)\,dp$. [given, F1, F3, F4, algebra]

2.1 Substitute the Maxwell relation [F2] into step 1.1 to obtain $dH=C_p\,dT+(V-T V_T|_{p,n})\,dp$. [F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Along a curve of constant $H$ and fixed $n$, step 2.1 gives $0=C_p\,dT+(V-T V_T|_{p,n})\,dp$. The assumed $(H,p,n)$ chart and $C_p>0$ therefore give $\mu_{JT}=(T V_T|_{p,n}-V)/C_p$. [given, F3, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Substitute $V_T|_{p,n}=V\alpha_p$ from [F3] to obtain $\mu_{JT}=V(T\alpha_p-1)/C_p$. Its units are $\mathrm{K\,Pa^{-1}}$ by [F5]. [F3, F5, step 3.1, algebra] ∎
sections.Remarks: An actual steady insulated throttle has constant upstream/downstream enthalpy only under an additional open-flow energy balance, negligible heat transfer and shaft work, and negligible kinetic and potential energy changes. This theorem is solely the derivative calculation on a specified equilibrium chart.

      url: https://phys.libretexts.org/Bookshelves/Thermodynamics_and_Statistical_Mechanics/Heat_and_Thermodynamics_(Tatum)/12:_Free_Energy/12.06:_The_Joule_and_Joule-Thomson_Coefficients
dependency_level: 10

## Statement

On a C2 Gibbs chart $G(T,p,n)$ at fixed composition $n$, with $T>0$, $V>0$, finite $C_p>0$, and a valid local inverse between $(T,p,n)$ and $(H,p,n)$, define the **Joule-Thomson coefficient** by

$$\mu_{JT}:=\left(\frac{\partial T}{\partial p}\right)_{H,n}.$$

Then

$$\mu_{JT}=\frac{T(\partial V/\partial T)_{p,n}-V}{C_p}=\frac{V(T\alpha_p-1)}{C_p},$$

where $\alpha_p=V^{-1}(\partial V/\partial T)_{p,n}$ and $C_p=(\partial H/\partial T)_{p,n}$ are the response functions of [[def-td-response-functions]]. This is a local derivative identity. It does not prove that a real throttle is isenthalpic or that a particular substance cools under expansion.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A fixed-composition open C2 chart with valid $(T,p,n)$ and $(H,p,n)$ coordinates, $T,V,C_p>0$, and the potentials defined in [[def-td-legendre-potentials]].

[F1] [[pthm-td-potential-differentials]]: On a valid chart, $dH=T\,ds+V\,dp+\sum_j\mu_j\,dn_j$ and $dG=-s\,dT+V\,dp+\sum_j\mu_j\,dn_j$.

[F2] [[pthm-td-maxwell-relations]]: For the Gibbs chart, $s_p|_{T,n}=-V_T|_{p,n}$.

[F3] [[def-td-response-functions]]: $C_p=H_T|_{p,n}$ and $\alpha_p=V^{-1}V_T|_{p,n}$ on a valid response chart.

[F4] [[def-td-legendre-potentials]]: $H=U+pV$ and $G=H-Ts$ on their local natural-variable charts.

[F5] [[def-td-si-quantities]]: $p$ is in pascals, $V$ in cubic metres, $U,H,G$ in joules, and $T$ in kelvins, with $\mathrm{Pa\,m^3=J}$.

## Proof

1.1 At fixed $n$, write $ds=s_T|_{p,n}\,dT+s_p|_{T,n}\,dp$ in [F1]. The enthalpy $H$ and chart are those of [F4]. Since $C_p=H_T|_{p,n}$ and $dH=T\,ds+V\,dp$, the coefficient of $dT$ gives $C_p=T s_T|_{p,n}$. Therefore $dH=C_p\,dT+(T s_p|_{T,n}+V)\,dp$. [given, F1, F3, F4, algebra]

2.1 Substitute the Maxwell relation [F2] into step 1.1 to obtain $dH=C_p\,dT+(V-T V_T|_{p,n})\,dp$. [F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Along a curve of constant $H$ and fixed $n$, step 2.1 gives $0=C_p\,dT+(V-T V_T|_{p,n})\,dp$. The assumed $(H,p,n)$ chart and $C_p>0$ therefore give $\mu_{JT}=(T V_T|_{p,n}-V)/C_p$. [given, F3, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Substitute $V_T|_{p,n}=V\alpha_p$ from [F3] to obtain $\mu_{JT}=V(T\alpha_p-1)/C_p$. Its units are $\mathrm{K\,Pa^{-1}}$ by [F5]. [F3, F5, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

An actual steady insulated throttle has constant upstream/downstream enthalpy only under an additional open-flow energy balance, negligible heat transfer and shaft work, and negligible kinetic and potential energy changes. This theorem is solely the derivative calculation on a specified equilibrium chart.

sections.Statement: Let $S$ have $N\ge2$ states, positive detailed-balance law $\pi$, and connected undirected rate graph as in [[def-td-detailed-balance-rate-model]]. For every strictly positive initial probability vector $p(0)$, the master equation has a unique strictly positive probability solution $p(t)$ for all $t\ge0$. The relative entropy $D(p(t)\Vert\pi)=\sum_i p_i(t)\log(p_i(t)/\pi_i)$ is nonincreasing, and $p_i(t)\to\pi_i$ for every state. No monotonicity of Shannon entropy $-\sum_i p_i\log p_i$ is asserted.
sections.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** A finite state set of size $N\ge2$, finite rates, a positive normalized detailed-balance vector $\pi$, and an initially strictly positive normalized vector $p(0)$.

[F1] [[def-td-detailed-balance-rate-model]]: $q_{ij}\ge0$ for $i\ne j$, $q_{ii}=-\sum_{j\ne i}q_{ij}$, and $\dot p_i=\sum_{j\ne i}(p_jq_{ji}-p_iq_{ij})$.

[F2] [[def-td-detailed-balance-rate-model]]: $a_{ij}:=\pi_iq_{ij}=\pi_jq_{ji}$ is positive on graph edges, and the graph is connected.

[F3] [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]: $\log(xy)=\log x+\log y$, $\log(1/x)=-\log x$, and $\log x\le0$ for $0<x\le1$.

[F4] [[thm-logarithm-derivative-and-integral]], [[thm-chain-rule]], and [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]: for $x>0$, $(\log x)'=1/x$, and the ordinary chain and finite-product rules differentiate the entropy sum.

[F5] [[thm-derivative-of-exponential]] and [[cor-mean-value-theorem]]: differentiate $e^{ct}$ and infer monotonicity on an interval from a nonpositive derivative.

[F6] [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-and-the-euclidean-norm]]: the finite Cauchy--Schwarz inequality bounds a sum of at most $N-1$ edge increments by $(N-1)$ times their squared sum.
sections.Proof:
**Given:** [F1]--[F6] and $p_i(0)>0$.

1.1 Put $c=1+\max_i\sum_{j\ne i}q_{ij}$ and $P=I+Q/c$, where $Q=(q_{ij})$. Then $P$ has nonnegative entries and row sums one. The series $p(t)=e^{-ct}\sum_{n=0}^\infty (ct)^n p(0)P^n/n!$ and its differentiated series converge uniformly on bounded time intervals; its coefficients are nonnegative and sum to one, so it is a probability vector, starts at $p(0)$, and differentiates to $\dot p=pQ$. Its $n=0$ term gives $p_i(t)\ge e^{-ct}p_i(0)>0$. For uniqueness, the difference $z$ of two solutions satisfies $z'=zQ$; with $C=\max_i\sum_j|q_{ij}|$ and $U(t)=\int_0^t\|z(s)\|_1ds$, one has $U'(t)=\|z(t)\|_1\le C U(t)$. Thus $(e^{-Ct}U(t))'\le0$ and $U(0)=0\le U(t)$ force $U=0$, hence $z=0$. [F1, F5, given, algebra]

2.1 With $r_i=p_i/\pi_i$, detailed balance gives $\dot p_i=\sum_{j\ne i}a_{ij}(r_j-r_i)$. By [F4], differentiating the finite entropy sum gives $D'=\sum_i\dot p_i(\log r_i+1)=\sum_i\dot p_i\log r_i$, since $\sum_i\dot p_i=0$. Pairing the $i,j$ terms gives $D'=-\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}a_{ij}(r_i-r_j)(\log r_i-\log r_j)\le0$: if $r_i\ge r_j$, then $\log r_i-\log r_j=-\log(r_j/r_i)\ge0$ by [F3], and the reversed order gives the same product sign. The mean value theorem [F5] on each compact time interval makes $D$ nonincreasing. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, step 1.1]

2.2 Set $u_i=r_i-1$, so $\sum_i\pi_i u_i=0$, and $V(t)=\sum_i\pi_i u_i^2$. Since $\dot u_i=\pi_i^{-1}\sum_{j\ne i}a_{ij}(u_j-u_i)$, differentiating and pairing the two orientations of each edge gives $V'=2\sum_i u_i\sum_{j\ne i}a_{ij}(u_j-u_i)=-2\sum_{\{i,j\}\in E}a_{ij}(u_i-u_j)^2$. [F1, F2, step 1.1]

3.1 Let $a_*=\min_{\{i,j\}\in E}a_{ij}>0$. Fix a root state and choose one simple path from it to each state; this is only a finite family of choices, obtainable successively, and each path has length at most $N-1$. Telescoping and [F6] give $(u_i-u_r)^2\le(N-1)\sum_{\{j,k\}\in E}(u_j-u_k)^2$. The zero-mean identity gives $u_r=-\sum_i\pi_i(u_i-u_r)$; expanding $\sum_i\pi_i[(u_i-u_r)-\sum_j\pi_j(u_j-u_r)]^2\ge0$ yields $u_r^2\le\sum_i\pi_i(u_i-u_r)^2$. Since $(x+y)^2\le2x^2+2y^2$ and $\sum_i\pi_i=1$, it follows that $V\le4(N-1)\sum_E(u_i-u_j)^2\le4(N-1)a_*^{-1}\sum_Ea_{ij}(u_i-u_j)^2$. [F2, F6, step 2.2, algebra]

4.1 Thus $V'\le-2\lambda V$ with $\lambda=a_*/[4(N-1)]>0$. By [F5], the derivative of $e^{2\lambda t}V(t)$ is nonpositive and that function is nonincreasing, so $V(t)\le e^{-2\lambda t}V(0)$. Since $\pi_i u_i(t)^2\le V(t)$ and $p_i-\pi_i=\pi_i u_i$, each $p_i(t)\to\pi_i$. [F5, step 2.2, step 3.1] ∎

sections.Statement:

sections.Statement: Under the hypotheses of [[pthm-td-finite-jarzynski]], the mean work obeys $\mathbb E_F W\ge\Delta F$. The conclusion concerns the path ensemble only; individual paths may have $W<\Delta F$.
sections.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** A finite-valued work random variable $W$ under the forward path law and $\beta>0$.

[F1] [[pthm-td-finite-jarzynski]]: $\mathbb E_F e^{-\beta W}=e^{-\beta\Delta F}$.

[F2] [[thm-exponential-two-point-convexity]]: $x\mapsto e^x$ is convex on $\mathbb R$.

[F3] [[thm-finite-jensen-inequality]]: for a finite probability vector $(p_j)$ and real values $(x_j)$, $e^{\sum p_jx_j}\le\sum p_je^{x_j}$.

[F4] [[thm-exponential-is-strictly-increasing]]: the exponential is strictly increasing on $\mathbb R$.
sections.Proof:
**Given:** [F1]--[F4].

1.1 Apply finite Jensen to the finitely many forward paths with $x_\omega=-\beta W(\omega)$ and weights $P_F(\omega)$. Then $e^{-\beta\mathbb E_F W}\le\mathbb E_F e^{-\beta W}=e^{-\beta\Delta F}$. [given, F1, F2, F3]

2.1 Strict increase of the exponential yields $-\beta\mathbb E_F W\le-\beta\Delta F$. Since $\beta>0$, multiplying by $-1/\beta$ reverses the order and gives $\mathbb E_F W\ge\Delta F$. [F4, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Under the hypotheses of [[pthm-td-finite-jarzynski]], the mean work obeys $\mathbb E_F W\ge\Delta F$. The conclusion concerns the path ensemble only; individual paths may have $W<\Delta F$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A finite-valued work random variable $W$ under the forward path law and $\beta>0$.

[F1] [[pthm-td-finite-jarzynski]]: $\mathbb E_F e^{-\beta W}=e^{-\beta\Delta F}$.

[F2] [[thm-exponential-two-point-convexity]]: $x\mapsto e^x$ is convex on $\mathbb R$.

[F3] [[thm-finite-jensen-inequality]]: for a finite probability vector $(p_j)$ and real values $(x_j)$, $e^{\sum p_jx_j}\le\sum p_je^{x_j}$.

[F4] [[thm-exponential-is-strictly-increasing]]: the exponential is strictly increasing on $\mathbb R$.

## Proof

**Given:** [F1]--[F4].

1.1 Apply finite Jensen to the finitely many forward paths with $x_\omega=-\beta W(\omega)$ and weights $P_F(\omega)$. Then $e^{-\beta\mathbb E_F W}\le\mathbb E_F e^{-\beta W}=e^{-\beta\Delta F}$. [given, F1, F2, F3]

2.1 Strict increase of the exponential yields $-\beta\mathbb E_F W\le-\beta\Delta F$. Since $\beta>0$, multiplying by $-1/\beta$ reverses the order and gives $\mathbb E_F W\ge\Delta F$. [F4, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

fm.title: Measurable canonical identities for a dimensionless reference measure
fm.physical_scope: Measurable energy models with a dimensionless reference measure, positive finite partition integral, and compact-parameter local integrable second-moment envelope; no claim is made for an arbitrary phase-space measure or unbounded energy without these hypotheses.

sections.Statement: Let $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ be a measure space with dimensionless reference measure, let $E:X\to\mathbb R\,\mathrm J$ be measurable, and let $J_\beta\subset(0,\infty)$ be open. Suppose $Z(\beta)=\int_Xe^{-\beta E}\,d\mu$ is positive and finite on $J_\beta$, and for each compact $K\subset J_\beta$ there is an integrable $G_K\ge0$ with $(1+|E|^2)e^{-\beta E}\le G_K$ for every $\beta\in K$. Under the canonical sampling assumption [[post-td-canonical-sampling]], define $p_\beta=e^{-\beta E}/Z$, $\langle E\rangle_\beta=\int E p_\beta\,d\mu$, and $\operatorname{Var}_\beta(E)=\int(E-\langle E\rangle_\beta)^2p_\beta\,d\mu$. Then $Z\in C^2$, $-\partial_\beta\log Z=\langle E\rangle_\beta$, $\partial_\beta^2\log Z=\operatorname{Var}_\beta(E)$, and the relative Gibbs entropy is finite with $S_\beta=-k_{\mathrm B}\int p_\beta\log p_\beta\,d\mu=k_{\mathrm B}(\log Z+\beta\langle E\rangle_\beta)$. Hence $F_{\mathrm{stat}}=-k_{\mathrm B}T\log Z=\langle E\rangle_\beta-TS_\beta$ for $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$.
sections.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** A dimensionless measure space, a measurable energy, positive finite partition integrals, the canonical density, and the stated local integrable envelope.

[F1] [[def-tdmath-measure-integral]]: measurable nonnegative energies and their nonnegative integrals are interpreted on the specified measure space; signed integrals require absolute integrability.

[F2] [[post-td-canonical-sampling]]: with $0<Z(\beta)<\infty$, the density $p_\beta=e^{-\beta E}/Z$ is the adopted canonical preparation relative to $\mu$.

[L1] [[thm-tdmath-measurable-canonical-identities]] (current batch 11 draft): under the stated $Z$ and compact-interval domination hypotheses, $Z$ is $C^2$, the mean and variance are its log derivatives, and the relative entropy is finite with value $\log Z+\beta\langle E\rangle$. Its full current proof was inspected; its draft status remains conditional.

[F3] [[def-td-si-quantities]]: $E$ and $\langle E\rangle$ are in joules, $T$ is in kelvins, and $k_{\mathrm B}$ is in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, so $\beta$ is in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$.

[A1] The reference measure is dimensionless, $Z$ is positive finite on the open interval, and $(1+|E|^2)e^{-\beta E}$ has the local integrable envelope stated in the Statement.
sections.Proof:
**Given:** The dimensionless reference measure, the measurable energy, the normalized canonical density, and the local envelope.

1.1 The hypotheses in the Statement match [L1], including positive finite $Z$ and the integrable envelope on each compact parameter interval. The density in [F2] is therefore normalized and has finite first and second energy moments. [F1, F2, F3, L1, A1]

2.1 Applying [L1] yields the $C^2$ partition integral, logarithmic mean and variance identities, and the finite relative entropy formula. Multiplying the dimensionless entropy by $k_{\mathrm B}$ gives $S_\beta=k_{\mathrm B}(\log Z+\beta\langle E\rangle_\beta)$; since $\beta k_{\mathrm B}=1/T$, rearranging gives $F_{\mathrm{stat}}=\langle E\rangle_\beta-TS_\beta=-k_{\mathrm B}T\log Z$. This conclusion is conditional on the draft mathematical supplier. [F2, F3, L1, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

sections.Statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the hypotheses and solution $T$ of [[pthm-td-constant-conductivity-neumann-existence]], let $V=|\Omega|=L_1L_2L_3$, define the spatial mean $\overline T(t)=V^{-1}\int_\Omega T(x,t)\,dx$, and put $E(t)=\int_\Omega|T(x,t)-\overline T(t)|^2\,dx$. With $a=k/c$ and $C_\Omega=\frac32\max_iL_i^2$, the mean is constant and
$$E(t)\le e^{-2at/C_\Omega}E(0)\qquad(t\ge0).$$
Thus this model solution converges exponentially to its initial spatial mean in $L^2(\Omega)$; no pointwise-uniform convergence rate is asserted.
sections.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** Countable Choice, the smooth positive solution and homogeneous Neumann boundary data from [[pthm-td-constant-conductivity-neumann-existence]], the rectangular mean-zero inequality on $\Omega$, and $a=k/c>0$.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function.

[F1] [[pthm-td-constant-conductivity-neumann-existence]]: $T_t=a\Delta T$ on $\Omega$, $\partial_nT=0$ on every face, and $T$ is $C^1$ in time and $C^2$ in space up to the boundary on finite intervals.

[F2] [[lem-td-rectangular-poincare]]: if $w$ has zero spatial mean, then $\int_\Omega w^2\le C_\Omega\int_\Omega|\nabla w|^2$ with $C_\Omega=\frac32\max_iL_i^2$.

[F3] [[thm-newton-leibniz-with-interior-derivative]]: a continuous function on a closed interval with an integrable interior derivative has endpoint increment equal to the derivative integral.

[F4] [[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]]: iterated Riemann integrals of continuous functions on product rectangles equal the multidimensional integral.
sections.Proof:
1.1 On each finite time interval the time derivative is continuous on the compact box, so its difference quotients converge uniformly under the spatial integral. By [F1] and [F4], coordinatewise application of [F3] gives $\overline T'(t)=aV^{-1}\int_\Omega\Delta T\,dx=0$: the integral of each second coordinate derivative is the difference of the corresponding first derivative on its two faces, and both normal derivatives vanish. Hence $\overline T(t)=\overline T(0)$. [A1, F1, F3, F4, given]

2.1 Set $w(x,t)=T(x,t)-\overline T(0)$. Then [F4] and step 1.1 give $\int_\Omega w=0$, while $w_t=a\Delta w$ and $\partial_nw=0$. Differentiating $E(t)=\int_\Omega w^2$ and using [F4], the product rule, and [F3] in each coordinate gives $E'(t)=2a\int_\Omega w\Delta w=-2a\int_\Omega|\nabla w|^2$; each endpoint term is $w\partial_nw=0$. [F1, F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Apply [F2] to $w(\cdot,t)$ in step 2.1. It gives $E(t)\le C_\Omega\int_\Omega|\nabla w|^2$, so $E'(t)\le-(2a/C_\Omega)E(t)$. [F2, step 2.1]

## Statement

Assume Countable Choice and the hypotheses and solution $T$ of [[pthm-td-constant-conductivity-neumann-existence]], let $V=|\Omega|=L_1L_2L_3$, define the spatial mean $\overline T(t)=V^{-1}\int_\Omega T(x,t)\,dx$, and put $E(t)=\int_\Omega|T(x,t)-\overline T(t)|^2\,dx$. With $a=k/c$ and $C_\Omega=\frac32\max_iL_i^2$, the mean is constant and
$$E(t)\le e^{-2at/C_\Omega}E(0)\qquad(t\ge0).$$
Thus this model solution converges exponentially to its initial spatial mean in $L^2(\Omega)$; no pointwise-uniform convergence rate is asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Countable Choice, the smooth positive solution and homogeneous Neumann boundary data from [[pthm-td-constant-conductivity-neumann-existence]], the rectangular mean-zero inequality on $\Omega$, and $a=k/c>0$.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]]: every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function.

[F1] [[pthm-td-constant-conductivity-neumann-existence]]: $T_t=a\Delta T$ on $\Omega$, $\partial_nT=0$ on every face, and $T$ is $C^1$ in time and $C^2$ in space up to the boundary on finite intervals.

[F2] [[lem-td-rectangular-poincare]]: if $w$ has zero spatial mean, then $\int_\Omega w^2\le C_\Omega\int_\Omega|\nabla w|^2$ with $C_\Omega=\frac32\max_iL_i^2$.

[F3] [[thm-newton-leibniz-with-interior-derivative]]: a continuous function on a closed interval with an integrable interior derivative has endpoint increment equal to the derivative integral.

[F4] [[thm-riemann-fubini-on-product-rectangles]]: iterated Riemann integrals of continuous functions on product rectangles equal the multidimensional integral.

## Proof


1.1 On each finite time interval the time derivative is continuous on the compact box, so its difference quotients converge uniformly under the spatial integral. By [F1] and [F4], coordinatewise application of [F3] gives $\overline T'(t)=aV^{-1}\int_\Omega\Delta T\,dx=0$: the integral of each second coordinate derivative is the difference of the corresponding first derivative on its two faces, and both normal derivatives vanish. Hence $\overline T(t)=\overline T(0)$. [A1, F1, F3, F4, given]

2.1 Set $w(x,t)=T(x,t)-\overline T(0)$. Then [F4] and step 1.1 give $\int_\Omega w=0$, while $w_t=a\Delta w$ and $\partial_nw=0$. Differentiating $E(t)=\int_\Omega w^2$ and using [F4], the product rule, and [F3] in each coordinate gives $E'(t)=2a\int_\Omega w\Delta w=-2a\int_\Omega|\nabla w|^2$; each endpoint term is $w\partial_nw=0$. [F1, F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Apply [F2] to $w(\cdot,t)$ in step 2.1. It gives $E(t)\le C_\Omega\int_\Omega|\nabla w|^2$, so $E'(t)\le-(2a/C_\Omega)E(t)$. [F2, step 2.1]

4.1 The product rule gives $(e^{2at/C_\Omega}E(t))'=e^{2at/C_\Omega}(E'(t)+(2a/C_\Omega)E(t))\le0$ by step 3.1. Integrating this derivative with [F3] from $0$ to $t$ yields $e^{2at/C_\Omega}E(t)\le E(0)$, which is the asserted estimate. [F3, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

fm.title: Differentials of the thermodynamic potentials
fm.physical_scope: Exact local differential identities on positive-temperature, C2, single-phase energy-representation charts with the stated Legendre coordinate maps invertible; no identity is asserted at singular response charts or phase boundaries.

references.title: Daniel Arovas, Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §2.7
