sections.Statement:
On a valid local energy-representation chart from [[pthm-td-local-energy-representation]], let $s,V,n_j,U,T,p,\mu_j$ and the potentials $H,F,G,\Omega$ be as defined in [[def-td-legendre-potentials]]. On every open neighborhood where the corresponding natural-coordinate maps have their stated $C^1$ inverses, the potentials are C2 and their differentials are

$$dU=T\,ds-p\,dV+\sum_{j=1}^r\mu_j\,dn_j,\qquad dH=T\,ds+V\,dp+\sum_{j=1}^r\mu_j\,dn_j,$$

$$dF=-s\,dT-p\,dV+\sum_{j=1}^r\mu_j\,dn_j,\qquad dG=-s\,dT+V\,dp+\sum_{j=1}^r\mu_j\,dn_j,$$

$$d\Omega=-s\,dT-p\,dV-\sum_{j=1}^r n_j\,d\mu_j.$$

All differentials are local state-function differentials. They do not assert that heat or work is an exact differential on process space.
sections.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** A fixed constitution $c$, an open C2 single-phase chart in coordinates $(s,V,n_1,\ldots,n_r)$, the local energy representation, and the valid natural-coordinate inverse charts named in the Statement. Use SI units: $U,H,F,G,\Omega$ in joules; $s$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$; $T$ in kelvins; $V$ in $\mathrm{m^3}$; $p$ in pascals; $n_j$ in moles; and $\mu_j$ in $\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$.

[F1] [[pthm-td-local-energy-representation]]: Its Statement gives $U_{c,s}=T_c$, $U_{c,V}=-p_c$, and $U_{c,n_j}=\mu_{c,j}$ on a local C2 chart. That supplier's Step 1 readiness record is authoring status, not independent proof acceptance, so this use remains conditional on its mathematical review.

[F2] [[def-td-legendre-potentials]]: $H=U+pV$, $F=U-Ts$, $G=F+pV$, and $\Omega=F-\sum_j\mu_jn_j$ on the stated inverse charts.

[F3] [[lem-tdmath-smooth-partial-legendre-transform-differential]]: For a C2 scalar function and an assumed C1 local inverse of its conjugate-coordinate map, the partial Legendre transform has differential $-u\cdot dx+D_zf\cdot dz$.
sections.Proof:
1.1 By [F1], the coordinate derivative of $U$ is $dU=U_s\,ds+U_V\,dV+\sum_jU_{n_j}\,dn_j=T\,ds-p\,dV+\sum_j\mu_j\,dn_j$. This step is conditional on the actual supplier interface and proof status recorded in [F1]. [given, F1, algebra]

2.1 Apply [F3] to the $V$ transform with conjugate coordinate $-p=U_V$ and to the $s$ transform with conjugate coordinate $T=U_s$. With the signs fixed in [F2], this gives $dH=T\,ds+V\,dp+\sum_j\mu_j\,dn_j$ and $dF=-s\,dT-p\,dV+\sum_j\mu_j\,dn_j$. [F2, F3, step 1.1]

2.2 Apply [F3] to the joint $(s,V)$ transform with conjugates $(T,-p)$. The definition [F2] has $G=U-Ts+pV$, so the transform differential is $dG=-s\,dT+V\,dp+\sum_j\mu_j\,dn_j$. [F2, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 Apply [F3] to the joint $(s,n)$ transform with conjugates $(T,\mu)$. The definition [F2] has $\Omega=U-Ts-\sum_j\mu_jn_j$, so the transform differential is $d\Omega=-s\,dT-p\,dV-\sum_jn_j\,d\mu_j$. [F2, F3, step 1.1] ∎

The supplier's proof remains a draft conditional on the registered batch-4 implicit-rank theorem; neither supplier readiness record is independent proof acceptance. This proof-status gap is recorded in batch 9 readiness evidence.

fm.title: Cesaro dephasing for a discrete trace-class quantum model
fm.physical_scope: A trace-class initial density and a self-adjoint quantum Hamiltonian with a complete discrete energy eigenfamily of finite multiplicity under the declared unitary dynamics; the result is a time-averaged state limit, not Gibbs preparation or pointwise relaxation.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §1.3.1 (printed pp. 18–19)

sections.Statement:
Assume AC. Let $H$ be a self-adjoint quantum Hamiltonian bounded below with a complete discrete energy eigenfamily of finite multiplicity, and let $\rho_0$ be any positive trace-class density operator of trace one. Let $\hbar>0$ be the assigned action constant in $\mathrm{J\,s}$, adopt the unitary dynamics $U_t=e^{-itH/\hbar}$ of [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]], and assume the trace-class Gibbs and local moment conditions of [[pthm-td-general-quantum-canonical-identities]] that supply this discrete eigenfamily. Then, conditional on the current batch-12 draft theorem [[thm-tdmath-discrete-quantum-cesaro-dephasing]], the Cesaro state
$$\bar\rho_\tau:=\frac1{\tau}\int_0^\tau U_t\rho_0U_t^*\,dt$$
converges in trace norm as $\tau\to\infty$ to $\rho_{\mathrm{diag}}=\sum_E P_E\rho_0P_E$, where $P_E$ is the spectral projection onto the full eigenspace of energy $E$. Coherences inside degenerate energy blocks remain. The limit need not be Gibbs, and no pointwise-in-time convergence or thermalization is asserted.
sections.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** A discrete self-adjoint Hamiltonian with finite-multiplicity energy eigenspaces, a trace-class density $\rho_0$, the declared unitary dynamics, and $\hbar$ in $\mathrm{J\,s}$.

[F2] [[pthm-td-general-quantum-canonical-identities]]: under the semibounded self-adjoint and trace-class Gibbs hypotheses with the stated local moment envelope, the Gibbs operator has a complete countable energy eigenfamily with finite multiplicity for each energy; this conclusion remains conditional on its current draft mathematical supplier.

[L1] [[thm-tdmath-discrete-quantum-cesaro-dephasing]] (current batch 12 draft): under AC, a complete finite-or-countable orthonormal eigenbasis of a semibounded self-adjoint operator, finite-dimensional energy eigenspaces, $\hbar>0$, and a positive trace-one trace-class density, the trace-norm Cesaro average converges to $\sum_E P_E\rho_0P_E$. The complete current proof was inspected; its Step 1 readiness is missing, so this premise remains conditional.

[A1] AC is assumed through [F2] and [L1]; $\tau>0$ is elapsed time in seconds and every phase $(E_i-E_j)t/\hbar$ is dimensionless.

[A2] $\rho_0$ is positive trace class with trace one, and $\hbar>0$ is the fixed action constant in $\mathrm{J\,s}$.

## Statement

Assume AC. Let $H$ be a self-adjoint quantum Hamiltonian bounded below with a complete discrete energy eigenfamily of finite multiplicity, and let $\rho_0$ be any positive trace-class density operator of trace one. Let $\hbar>0$ be the assigned action constant in $\mathrm{J\,s}$, adopt the unitary dynamics $U_t=e^{-itH/\hbar}$ of [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]], and assume the trace-class Gibbs and local moment conditions of [[pthm-td-general-quantum-canonical-identities]] that supply this discrete eigenfamily. Then, conditional on the current batch-12 draft theorem [[thm-tdmath-discrete-quantum-cesaro-dephasing]], the Cesaro state
$$\bar\rho_\tau:=\frac1{\tau}\int_0^\tau U_t\rho_0U_t^*\,dt$$
converges in trace norm as $\tau\to\infty$ to $\rho_{\mathrm{diag}}=\sum_E P_E\rho_0P_E$, where $P_E$ is the spectral projection onto the full eigenspace of energy $E$. Coherences inside degenerate energy blocks remain. The limit need not be Gibbs, and no pointwise-in-time convergence or thermalization is asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A discrete self-adjoint Hamiltonian with finite-multiplicity energy eigenspaces, a trace-class density $\rho_0$, the declared unitary dynamics, and $\hbar$ in $\mathrm{J\,s}$.

[F1] [[post-nrqm-framework-autonomous-dynamics]] and [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]: the declared closed-system state evolves by $\rho(t)=U_t\rho_0U_t^*$ with $U_t=e^{-itH/\hbar}$ and unitary group law.

[F2] [[pthm-td-general-quantum-canonical-identities]]: under the semibounded self-adjoint and trace-class Gibbs hypotheses with the stated local moment envelope, the Gibbs operator has a complete countable energy eigenfamily with finite multiplicity for each energy; this conclusion remains conditional on its current draft mathematical supplier.

[L1] [[thm-tdmath-discrete-quantum-cesaro-dephasing]] (current batch 12 draft): under AC, a complete finite-or-countable orthonormal eigenbasis of a semibounded self-adjoint operator, finite-dimensional energy eigenspaces, $\hbar>0$, and a positive trace-one trace-class density, the trace-norm Cesaro average converges to $\sum_E P_E\rho_0P_E$. The complete current proof was inspected; its Step 1 readiness is missing, so this premise remains conditional.

[A1] AC is assumed through [F2] and [L1]; $\tau>0$ is elapsed time in seconds and every phase $(E_i-E_j)t/\hbar$ is dimensionless.

[A2] $\rho_0$ is positive trace class with trace one, and $\hbar>0$ is the fixed action constant in $\mathrm{J\,s}$.

## Proof

**Given:** The trace-class state, the discrete energy basis, the unitary dynamics, and the current draft trace-norm Cesaro theorem.

1.1 By [F2], the trace-class Gibbs and local moment assumptions supply a complete countable energy eigenbasis with finite-dimensional eigenspaces; [A1] supplies AC and [A2] supplies the positive trace-one initial density and action-unit convention. Together with the semibounded self-adjoint Hamiltonian in the Statement, these are the hypotheses of [L1], and [F1] specifies the same unitary orbit. [F1, F2, L1, A1, A2]

2.1 Apply the current draft result [L1] to the matched inputs in step 1.1. It yields $\bar\rho_\tau\to\sum_E P_E\rho_0P_E$ in trace norm with the entire degenerate blocks retained. The limit depends on $\rho_0$, so no Gibbs or pointwise-time conclusion follows. This use remains conditional until [L1] has current Step 1 readiness. [F1, F2, L1, step 1.1] ∎

sections.Statement: For the reset model of [[def-td-finite-memory-reset-model]], assume (i) the memory-register thermodynamic entropy is $k_{\mathrm B}H(M,R)$ at both endpoints, (ii) a single ideal reservoir remains at fixed $T_b>0$ kelvin and receives heat $Q_b$, (iii) the memory-register endpoint energy is unchanged so the adopted first-law convention gives work on the system $W=Q_b$, and (iv) the total entropy change obeys $\Delta S_{\mathrm{memory+register}}+Q_b/T_b\ge0$. Then $W\ge k_{\mathrm B}T_bH(M|R)$. Equality is not asserted without a separately specified reversible implementation.
sections.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** Finite sets $M,R$, a joint law, the reset map, $T_b>0$, work positive on the system, and heat $Q_b$ positive into the bath.

[F1] [[def-td-finite-memory-reset-model]]: the reset makes $M'=m_0$ and preserves the register marginal $a_r$.

[F2] [[lem-tdmath-conditional-memory-entropy]]: actual current carrier status is draft; its inspected statement for finite joint laws gives $H(M,R)=H(R)+H(M|R)$ and $H(M|R)\ge0$. Its proof directly expands $p(m,r)=a_rq(m|r)$ and treats zero marginals separately.

[A1] Adopt the finite-memory entropy identification $S_{\mathrm{memory+register}}=k_{\mathrm B}H(M,R)$ at each endpoint.

[A2] Adopt an ideal fixed-temperature bath with $T_b>0$ and entropy change $Q_b/T_b$ for heat delivered to it.

[A3] Adopt unchanged endpoint energy and the convention $W=Q_b$ for work on the memory-register system and heat delivered to the bath.

[A4] Adopt total entropy nondecrease for this reset process: $\Delta S_{\mathrm{memory+register}}+Q_b/T_b\ge0$.

**Given:** [F1], [F2], and physical assumptions [A1]--[A4].

1.1 Initially the memory-register entropy is $k_{\mathrm B}[H(R)+H(M|R)]$ by [F2] and [A1]. After reset, the memory is deterministic conditional on each register value, so $H(M'|R)=0$; applying the same finite entropy chain rule gives final entropy $k_{\mathrm B}H(R)$. [F1, F2, A1, algebra]

[A1, A2, A3, A4, step 2.1] ∎

fm.physical_scope: Classical positional Borel pair systems in dimension at least two; van Hove free-wall limits require superstability and regularity, while deterministic exterior limits additionally require a genuine positive divergent core in the supplier's infinity norm and a fixed uniformly tempered exterior class.

sections.Statement:
Assume AC, as required by the current mathematical definition and its shape suppliers. Let $d\geq2$, $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$, $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$, and assume $\widehat\varphi$ is Borel measurable and superstable and regular as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. Use $\widehat H=H/E_0$ and $\widehat\beta=E_0(k_BT)^{-1}>0$ in the mathematical rates. Let $(\Lambda_k)$ be a van Hove sequence as in [[def-td-admissible-van-hove-and-tempered-exterior]]. First, for free walls, the positional grand pressure along $\Lambda_k$ converges to the free-cube pressure of [[pthm-td-stable-tempered-free-cube-grand-pressure]]. For any positive interior attainable density $\rho$ and exact integers $N_k$ with $N_k/|\Lambda_k|\to\rho$, the exact-$N_k$ free-wall canonical log-partition rate converges to the same cube canonical rate. These two shape statements require superstability and regularity; stability alone is not asserted to suffice for arbitrary van Hove shapes.

Second, strengthen the potential hypothesis: for some $r_0>0$, $\widehat\varphi(x)\geq\widehat\chi(\|x\|_\infty)>0$ whenever $0<\|x\|_\infty\leq r_0$, where $\widehat\chi$ is nonincreasing and $\int_0^{r_0}\widehat\chi(r)r^{d-1}\,dr=+\infty$. For each fixed $t<\infty$, the free-wall grand pressure in $\Lambda_n$ with exterior $\zeta\in\Omega(t)$ then converges uniformly in $\zeta$ to the same free-cube pressure. The exterior interaction is the deterministic positional term of [[def-td-admissible-van-hove-and-tempered-exterior]], not a volume-filling external field. This genuine divergent-core condition is the exact stronger hypothesis of the current exterior supplier; it is not inferred from superstability or replaced by a weaker source condition.
sections.Facts & Assumptions:
[F1] [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]]: $\varphi$ is even measurable, stable, and has an integrable decreasing tail. With $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$, $\widehat H=H/E_0$ and $\widehat\beta=E_0(k_BT)^{-1}$ leave each Boltzmann factor unchanged.

[F2] [[def-td-admissible-van-hove-and-tempered-exterior]]: van Hove geometry controls fixed-width boundary layers; $\Omega(t)$ fixes a uniform square-count bound on the exterior configuration. The local Euclidean and mathematical $\ell^\infty$ boundary-layer conditions agree for van Hove sequences because $\|x\|_\infty\leq|x|_2\leq\sqrt d\|x\|_\infty$ and the definition quantifies over every fixed layer width.

[A1] [[post-td-equilibrium-ensemble-sampling]]: all grand and canonical laws are positional and use the adopted indistinguishable measure.

[L0] [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]: the current definition assumes AC, requires an even Borel potential, a stable-plus-nonnegative superstable splitting with a positive lower bound on an $\ell^\infty$-ball, and its lower/upper regularity tails; it separately defines the genuine divergent positive core. The definition carrier is present as a draft; its proof-contract entry passes, but no current batch-18 Step 1 decision is recorded.


[L1] [[thm-tdmath-superstable-van-hove-pressure]]: the current statement gives free-wall grand-pressure convergence to the free-cube rate on every van Hove sequence under superstability and regularity; its text expressly does not assert stability alone. The item and draft proof text are present and the scoped batch-18 proof-contract check passes, but no Step 1 decision is recorded; this use remains conditional.

[L2] [[thm-tdmath-van-hove-fixed-n-limit]]: the current statement gives the free-wall exact-$N_k$ positional log-partition rate on van Hove regions for $N_k/|\Lambda_k|\to\rho$ at a positive interior attainable density, under superstability and regularity. Its current draft statement/proof carrier and scoped batch-18 proof-contract entry pass; no Step 1 decision is recorded; this use remains conditional.

[L3] [[thm-tdmath-uniform-tempered-exterior-pressure]]: the current statement gives uniform free-wall grand-pressure convergence for each fixed exterior class $\Omega(t)$ under stable regularity and the genuine divergent positive core $\widehat\varphi(x)\geq\widehat\chi(\|x\|_\infty)$ with divergent radial integral. Its item and draft proof text are present and the scoped batch-18 proof-contract check passes, but no Step 1 decision is recorded; this use remains conditional.
sections.Proof:
**Given:** The physical finite-volume law and numerical energy conversion, AC, definitions of geometry and exterior preparation in [F2], and the actual draft mathematical supplier statements [L1]–[L3]. Their unresolved proof status remains conditional input.

1.1 Under the Borel superstable regular hypotheses of [L0] and the physical pair assumptions [F1], the finite-dimensional norm bounds in [F2] transfer the local van Hove sequence to the supplier's $\ell^\infty$ boundary convention. The free-wall grand-pressure result then identifies its limit with the free-cube pressure. The physical grand normalizer and pressure are the ones fixed in [A1] and the earlier free-cube theorem. [given, F1, F2, A1, L0, L1]

2.1 For an interior attainable $\rho$ and the stated $N_k$, [L2] gives convergence of the exact-$N_k$ free-wall canonical log-partition rate to the same cube canonical rate. Its boundary-layer hypothesis is precisely the van Hove condition in [F2]. [given, F1, F2, A1, L2, step 1.1]

2.2 Under the additional positive divergent-core condition defined in [L0], every $\zeta\in\Omega(t)$ meets the fixed exterior class in [F2]; [L3] gives uniform convergence of its grand pressure to the free-cube pressure. This conclusion is uniform only for the fixed $t$ class and does not cover a potential applied throughout a volume. [given, F1, F2, A1, L0, L3, step 1.1]

3.1 Combining the three conditional limits proves exactly the two stated boundary regimes. The superstability and genuine-core assumptions remain distinct, so neither result is extended to stability alone or to arbitrary external fields. [step 1.1, step 2.1, step 2.2, L1, L2, L3] ∎

sections.Statement:
Fix $C\ge1$ species and $R\ge1$ declared internal reaction extents. Let $\nu\in\mathbb R^{C\times R}$ be the dimensionless stoichiometric matrix, let $n^0\in[0,\infty)^C$ have units mol, and let $\xi\in\mathbb R^R$ have units mol. The amount vector is $n(\xi)=n^0+\nu\xi$, and the nonnegative-amount feasible extent set is
$$
\mathcal F_\nu:=\{\xi\in\mathbb R^R:n^0+\nu\xi\in[0,\infty)^C\}.
$$
Fix $T_0>0$ and $p_0$ in a declared natural-variable chart. Let $\Phi(\xi)$ be the constrained Gibbs potential on an open neighborhood $U$ of an equilibrium extent $\xi_*$, and assume the model supplies a finite $C^1$ extension through every zero-amount boundary point under consideration. On $U$, assume
$$
D\Phi(\xi)[h]=\sum_{j=1}^C\mu_j(\xi)(\nu h)_j=(\nu^{\mathsf T}\mu(\xi))\cdot h,
$$

fm.title: Ideal-bath refrigerator coefficient-of-performance bound
fm.physical_scope: Conditional cooling coefficient-of-performance bound for an admitted closed refrigerator cycle between positive-temperature ideal baths inside an isolated compound with an ideal work store; finite reservoirs, unlisted transfers, and empirical appliance performance are excluded.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete Chapter 4 lecture-note PDF, §§4.3.1–4.3.3
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, Chapter 2, §§2.5.2–2.5.3

sections.Statement:
Let an admitted refrigerator cycle in the sense of [[def-td-reservoir-cycle]] operate between fixed ideal-bath temperatures $0<T_c<T_h$, extract $Q_c>0$ from the cold bath, reject $Q_h>0$ to the hot bath, and consume $W_{\mathrm{in}}>0$. Define its cooling coefficient of performance by $\mathrm{COP}_R=Q_c/W_{\mathrm{in}}$. Then
$
\mathrm{COP}_R\le\frac{T_c}{T_h-T_c}.
$
Equality holds exactly when the total entropy change of the isolated compound is zero. A reversible cycle in the stated boundary model saturates the bound; no converse about reversibility is asserted.
sections.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** A cyclic working system with $0<T_c<T_h$, $Q_c>0$, $Q_h>0$, $W_{\mathrm{in}}>0$, no unlisted transfers, and the full working system, baths, and work store inside the declared isolated compound.

[F1] [[def-td-reservoir-cycle]]: In refrigerator mode $Q[P]=Q_c-Q_h$, $W_{\mathrm{on}}[P]=W_{\mathrm{in}}$, the cold and hot bath energy changes are $-Q_c$ and $+Q_h$, their endpoint entropy changes are $-Q_c/T_c$ and $+Q_h/T_h$, and the work store has zero entropy change. The full compound has the admitted equilibrium endpoint record and additive entropy split required by the definition.

[F2] [[post-td-first-law-energy]]: For an admitted closed fixed-constitution process with zero endpoint changes in separately tracked center-of-mass kinetic and external-potential energies, $\Delta U=Q[P]+W_{\mathrm{on}}[P]$.

[F3] [[post-td-macroscopic-second-law]]: For an admitted isolated compound process with equilibrium endpoints and the declared additive total entropy, $\Delta S_{\mathrm{tot}}\ge0$; an admitted reversible operation has $\Delta S_{\mathrm{tot}}=0$.
sections.Proof:
**Given:** The fixed-bath cycle hypotheses in the Statement and the heat/work signs in [F1].

1.1 The working system returns to its initial state, so $\Delta U=0$. Applying [F2] with [F1] gives $0=Q_c-Q_h+W_{\mathrm{in}}$, hence $Q_h=Q_c+W_{\mathrm{in}}$. [given, F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 The cold bath loses $Q_c$, the hot bath gains $Q_h$, and their entropy slopes are constant. Thus their entropy changes are $-Q_c/T_c$ and $Q_h/T_h$. The working system and work store have zero entropy change, so [F3] gives
$
-\frac{Q_c}{T_c}+\frac{Q_h}{T_h}=\Delta S_{\mathrm{tot}}\ge0.
$
[given, F1, F3, algebra]

2.1 Since $T_c,T_h>0$, step 1.2 gives $Q_h\ge Q_cT_h/T_c$. Substituting $Q_h=Q_c+W_{\mathrm{in}}$ from step 1.1 yields
$
W_{\mathrm{in}}\ge Q_c\frac{T_h-T_c}{T_c}.
$
[given, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 Divide by $W_{\mathrm{in}}>0$ and use $T_h-T_c>0$ to obtain $\mathrm{COP}_R\le T_c/(T_h-T_c)$. Equality is equivalent to $\Delta S_{\mathrm{tot}}=0$; a reversible cycle has this property by [F3]. [given, F3, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

fm.title: Local regular dimension of a reacting Gibbs phase-coexistence manifold
fm.physical_scope: Interior compositions of finitely many C1 intensive phase branches with energy, volume, all listed species exchanges, and internal reactions allowed in every phase, at a solution where the combined coexistence-and-affinity Jacobian has a nonsingular minor; phase amounts, boundaries, singular critical points, and externally fixed variables are excluded.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, author-hosted complete lecture notes, §5.1.1
Konstantin K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics: Statistical Mechanics, §4.1 First-order phase transitions

sections.Statement:
Assume the entropy of each phase is $C^2$ on its physical state chart and its derivative-defined temperature at the endpoint is finite and positive. The equation-set dimension below concerns this smooth interior state only.

Let $C\ge1$ be the number of named species, $P\ge1$ the number of coexisting phase branches, and $R\ge0$ the number of independent internal reaction directions. Consider an attained global entropy-maximizing endpoint on the exact feasible set of [[def-td-isolated-compound-feasible-set]]. For each phase $\alpha$, use an intensive phase branch from [[def-td-phase-and-coexistence-domain]] and an interior composition $x^\alpha\in\Delta_{C-1}^{\circ}$. Let each branch chemical-potential map
$$
\mu^\alpha(T,p,x^\alpha)=(\mu_1^\alpha,\ldots,\mu_C^\alpha)
$$
be $C^1$ on a common open domain
$$
\mathcal U=(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R\times(\Delta_{C-1}^{\circ})^P \subseteq\mathbb R^{\,n},\qquad n=2+P(C-1).
$$
Assume energy, volume, and every named species can be exchanged between every phase pair in both directions, and every listed reaction direction is feasible in both extent directions in every phase while that phase's energy, volume, other reaction extents, and all other phase coordinates are held fixed at the coexistence point. Let $\nu^1,\ldots,\nu^R\in\mathbb R^C$ be linearly independent, dimensionless stoichiometric vectors, with extents measured in moles. Phase equilibrium imposes $\mu_i^\alpha-\mu_i^1=0$ for $1\le i\le C$, $2\le\alpha\le P$; internal reaction equilibrium imposes $(\nu^r)^{\mathsf T}\mu^\alpha=0$ in every phase for $1\le r\le R$. On the phase-equality locus these are the same $R$ equations in each phase, so count them once using phase 1. Put $q:=C(P-1)$ and $m:=q+R$. If $m=0$ (equivalently $P=1,R=0$), no equation is imposed and the local zero set is the whole chart, of dimension $n=C+1=C-P+2-R$. If $m\ge1$ and the combined equation map has an invertible $m\times m$ derivative minor at the solution, with $m\le n$, then the local zero set of these first-order coexistence-and-affinity equations is a graph of dimension
$$
n-q-R=C-P+2-R.
$$
This is the dimension of the equation zero set in intensive coordinates only; phase amounts and their extensive conservation constraints are not counted, and the actual stable-coexistence set may be a proper subset after additional stability constraints. If the nonsingular-minor condition fails, no dimension formula is asserted.
sections.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** Finite integers $C,P,R$, the open positive-temperature, interior-composition chart, C1 branch chemical-potential maps, a coexistence solution, the pairwise exchange assumptions, independent stoichiometric directions, and the stated nonsingular-minor hypothesis. Mole fractions are dimensionless; each $\mu_i^\alpha$ has units $\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$.

[A1] [[def-td-phase-and-coexistence-domain]]: Each branch is a model-supplied C1 intensive phase chart, so derivative-defined chemical potentials are independent of the phase amount and are C1 maps of $(T,p,x^\alpha)$.

[A2] Regularity hypothesis: Each phase entropy is C2 in its physical state coordinates at the endpoint, and each derivative-defined temperature is finite and positive.

[F1] [[pthm-td-intensive-coexistence-conditions]]: At an attained entropy-maximizing coexistence point, bilateral energy and volume exchange imply equal positive temperature and pressure, and bilateral species exchange implies equal derivative-defined chemical potentials across phases.

[F2] [[post-td-entropy-maximum]] and [[post-td-bulk-additivity]]: The total entropy of the separated phases is the sum of their state entropies, and the adopted stable endpoint is a global maximum on its exact feasible set.

[F3] [[def-td-temperature-pressure-chemical-potential]]: On each single-phase chart, $S_{n_j}=-\mu_j/T$ at fixed energy, volume, and other species amounts; branch temperatures are positive.

[L1] [[thm-tdmath-phase-dimension]]: For C1 chemical-potential maps on the stated open intensive composition chart, the zero set of the phase-equality equations and $R$ independent affinity equations has local dimension $2+P(C-1)-C(P-1)-R$ when the combined equation map has an invertible square derivative minor of size $C(P-1)+R$. The current batch-4 carrier and its proof contract are registered; the item remains a draft and is not independently accepted.
sections.Proof:
1.1 For $P\ge2$, define the phase-equality components $F_{i,\alpha}:=\mu_i^\alpha-\mu_i^1$ for $1\le i\le C$, $2\le\alpha\le P$. There are exactly $q=C(P-1)$ such scalar equations. By [A1], each $\mu_i^\alpha$ is C1 on the common open domain, so their finite differences are C1. By [F1], these equations hold at the stated physical coexistence point when the corresponding species exchanges are admitted; [A2] supplies the entropy regularity and positive temperatures required by that supplier. [given, A1, A2, F1, algebra]

1.2 Fix any phase $\alpha$ and reaction direction $\nu^r$. Vary only that phase's species amounts as $n^\alpha(t)=n^{\alpha,*}+t\nu^r$, holding its energy and volume and all other phase coordinates fixed; $t$ is a small extent in moles. By the stated bilateral feasibility, this curve is admitted for both signs of sufficiently small $t$. The total entropy has a local maximum at $t=0$ by [F2]. Its differentiability there follows from [A2]. The right difference quotients are nonpositive and the left difference quotients are nonnegative; the derivative is therefore zero. Additivity and [F3] give
$$
0=\frac{dS_{\mathrm{tot}}}{dt}(0)=\sum_j S_{\alpha,n_j}\nu_j^r=-\frac{(\nu^r)^{\mathsf T}\mu^\alpha}{T}.
$$
Since $T>0$, $(\nu^r)^{\mathsf T}\mu^\alpha=0$ in every phase. The equations are C1 because they are finite linear combinations of the C1 branch maps. By [F1], phase equalities make the affinity equation identical across phases, so count only the $R$ equations in phase 1. The combined map therefore has $q+R$ equations. [given, A1, A2, F1, F2, F3, construct, algebra]

1.3 The ambient coordinate dimension is $n=2+P(C-1)$. If $q+R=0$, then $P=1$ and $R=0$, so there are no phase-equality or reaction-affinity equations. The local zero set is all of the open chart and has dimension $n=2+(C-1)=C-P+2-R$. [given, algebra]

2.1 If $q+R\ge1$, apply [L1] to the combined C1 equation map using the stated invertible minor. Its local zero set has dimension
$$
n-q-R=2+P(C-1)-C(P-1)-R=C-P+2-R.
$$
This conclusion is conditional on the full-rank minor; it does not follow from equation counting alone. Additional stability constraints may reduce the physical coexistence set. [given, L1, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra] ∎
sections.Remarks: The zero-reaction case is $R=0$. On composition boundaries the open-simplex chart fails; for reactions there, one-sided tangent inequalities replace the interior affinity equalities.

## Statement

Assume the entropy of each phase is $C^2$ on its physical state chart and its derivative-defined temperature at the endpoint is finite and positive. The equation-set dimension below concerns this smooth interior state only.

Let $C\ge1$ be the number of named species, $P\ge1$ the number of coexisting phase branches, and $R\ge0$ the number of independent internal reaction directions. Consider an attained global entropy-maximizing endpoint on the exact feasible set of [[def-td-isolated-compound-feasible-set]]. For each phase $\alpha$, use an intensive phase branch from [[def-td-phase-and-coexistence-domain]] and an interior composition $x^\alpha\in\Delta_{C-1}^{\circ}$. Let each branch chemical-potential map
$$
\mu^\alpha(T,p,x^\alpha)=(\mu_1^\alpha,\ldots,\mu_C^\alpha)
$$
be $C^1$ on a common open domain
$$
\mathcal U=(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R\times(\Delta_{C-1}^{\circ})^P \subseteq\mathbb R^{\,n},\qquad n=2+P(C-1).
$$
Assume energy, volume, and every named species can be exchanged between every phase pair in both directions, and every listed reaction direction is feasible in both extent directions in every phase while that phase's energy, volume, other reaction extents, and all other phase coordinates are held fixed at the coexistence point. Let $\nu^1,\ldots,\nu^R\in\mathbb R^C$ be linearly independent, dimensionless stoichiometric vectors, with extents measured in moles. Phase equilibrium imposes $\mu_i^\alpha-\mu_i^1=0$ for $1\le i\le C$, $2\le\alpha\le P$; internal reaction equilibrium imposes $(\nu^r)^{\mathsf T}\mu^\alpha=0$ in every phase for $1\le r\le R$. On the phase-equality locus these are the same $R$ equations in each phase, so count them once using phase 1. Put $q:=C(P-1)$ and $m:=q+R$. If $m=0$ (equivalently $P=1,R=0$), no equation is imposed and the local zero set is the whole chart, of dimension $n=C+1=C-P+2-R$. If $m\ge1$ and the combined equation map has an invertible $m\times m$ derivative minor at the solution, with $m\le n$, then the local zero set of these first-order coexistence-and-affinity equations is a graph of dimension
$$
n-q-R=C-P+2-R.
$$
This is the dimension of the equation zero set in intensive coordinates only; phase amounts and their extensive conservation constraints are not counted, and the actual stable-coexistence set may be a proper subset after additional stability constraints. If the nonsingular-minor condition fails, no dimension formula is asserted.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Finite integers $C,P,R$, the open positive-temperature, interior-composition chart, C1 branch chemical-potential maps, a coexistence solution, the pairwise exchange assumptions, independent stoichiometric directions, and the stated nonsingular-minor hypothesis. Mole fractions are dimensionless; each $\mu_i^\alpha$ has units $\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$.

[A1] [[def-td-phase-and-coexistence-domain]]: Each branch is a model-supplied C1 intensive phase chart, so derivative-defined chemical potentials are independent of the phase amount and are C1 maps of $(T,p,x^\alpha)$.

[A2] Regularity hypothesis: Each phase entropy is C2 in its physical state coordinates at the endpoint, and each derivative-defined temperature is finite and positive.

[F1] [[pthm-td-intensive-coexistence-conditions]]: At an attained entropy-maximizing coexistence point, bilateral energy and volume exchange imply equal positive temperature and pressure, and bilateral species exchange implies equal derivative-defined chemical potentials across phases.

[F2] [[post-td-entropy-maximum]] and [[post-td-bulk-additivity]]: The total entropy of the separated phases is the sum of their state entropies, and the adopted stable endpoint is a global maximum on its exact feasible set.

[F3] [[def-td-temperature-pressure-chemical-potential]]: On each single-phase chart, $S_{n_j}=-\mu_j/T$ at fixed energy, volume, and other species amounts; branch temperatures are positive.

[L1] [[thm-tdmath-phase-dimension]]: For C1 chemical-potential maps on the stated open intensive composition chart, the zero set of the phase-equality equations and $R$ independent affinity equations has local dimension $2+P(C-1)-C(P-1)-R$ when the combined equation map has an invertible square derivative minor of size $C(P-1)+R$. The current batch-4 carrier and its proof contract are registered; the item remains a draft and is not independently accepted.

## Proof

1.1 For $P\ge2$, define the phase-equality components $F_{i,\alpha}:=\mu_i^\alpha-\mu_i^1$ for $1\le i\le C$, $2\le\alpha\le P$. There are exactly $q=C(P-1)$ such scalar equations. By [A1], each $\mu_i^\alpha$ is C1 on the common open domain, so their finite differences are C1. By [F1], these equations hold at the stated physical coexistence point when the corresponding species exchanges are admitted; [A2] supplies the entropy regularity and positive temperatures required by that supplier. [given, A1, A2, F1, algebra]

1.2 Fix any phase $\alpha$ and reaction direction $\nu^r$. Vary only that phase's species amounts as $n^\alpha(t)=n^{\alpha,*}+t\nu^r$, holding its energy and volume and all other phase coordinates fixed; $t$ is a small extent in moles. By the stated bilateral feasibility, this curve is admitted for both signs of sufficiently small $t$. The total entropy has a local maximum at $t=0$ by [F2]. Its differentiability there follows from [A2]. The right difference quotients are nonpositive and the left difference quotients are nonnegative; the derivative is therefore zero. Additivity and [F3] give
$$
0=\frac{dS_{\mathrm{tot}}}{dt}(0)=\sum_j S_{\alpha,n_j}\nu_j^r=-\frac{(\nu^r)^{\mathsf T}\mu^\alpha}{T}.
$$
Since $T>0$, $(\nu^r)^{\mathsf T}\mu^\alpha=0$ in every phase. The equations are C1 because they are finite linear combinations of the C1 branch maps. By [F1], phase equalities make the affinity equation identical across phases, so count only the $R$ equations in phase 1. The combined map therefore has $q+R$ equations. [given, A1, A2, F1, F2, F3, construct, algebra]

1.3 The ambient coordinate dimension is $n=2+P(C-1)$. If $q+R=0$, then $P=1$ and $R=0$, so there are no phase-equality or reaction-affinity equations. The local zero set is all of the open chart and has dimension $n=2+(C-1)=C-P+2-R$. [given, algebra]

2.1 If $q+R\ge1$, apply [L1] to the combined C1 equation map using the stated invertible minor. Its local zero set has dimension
$$
n-q-R=2+P(C-1)-C(P-1)-R=C-P+2-R.
$$
This conclusion is conditional on the full-rank minor; it does not follow from equation counting alone. Additional stability constraints may reduce the physical coexistence set. [given, L1, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

The zero-reaction case is $R=0$. On composition boundaries the open-simplex chart fails; for reactions there, one-sided tangent inequalities replace the interior affinity equalities.

fm.title: Helmholtz and Gibbs potential minimum principles for ideal reservoirs
fm.physical_scope: Conditional endpoint deductions for closed, fixed-composition macroscopic systems coupled to the explicitly defined ideal thermal and pressure reservoirs; other work coordinates, open matter flow, and nonideal finite reservoirs are excluded.

references.title: Daniel Arovas, Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §2.7

sections.Statement:
Fix a closed macroscopic system with composition fixed and two admitted equilibrium endpoints. In the fixed-volume model, couple it only to an ideal thermal reservoir at constant $T_0>0$. In the fixed-pressure model, also couple it to an ideal pressure store at constant $p_0>0$. Define the constrained potentials

$$F_{T_0}(x):=U(x)-T_0S(x),\qquad G_{T_0,p_0}(x):=U(x)+p_0V(x)-T_0S(x).$$

Assume the ideal-reservoir bookkeeping specified in [A1]–[A3] of Facts & Assumptions and the adopted isolated-compound second law [[post-td-macroscopic-second-law]]. Then along every admitted spontaneous endpoint change at fixed volume, $F_{T_0}$ does not increase; at fixed pressure, $G_{T_0,p_0}$ does not increase. If an endpoint is an attained global entropy maximum on the same feasible set, the corresponding constrained potential attains a global minimum there. If the system endpoint is on its $T=T_0$ or $(T,p)=(T_0,p_0)$ natural-variable chart, these constrained functions agree with the Helmholtz or Gibbs potentials of [[def-td-legendre-potentials]].

The statement is conditional on the ideal bath/load model and is not a claim that every physical process has such a reservoir or reaches the minimum.
sections.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** A fixed composition, an explicit feasible endpoint set for a closed system plus its named reservoirs, equilibrium endpoints, fixed excluded kinetic and external-field energy changes, and the following ideal reservoir model. Energies are in joules, entropy in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, $T_0$ in kelvins, $V$ in $\mathrm{m^3}$, and $p_0$ in pascals.

[A1] Ideal thermal reservoir: its energy $E_R$ ranges in an open interval and its entropy is $S_R(E_R)=S_{R,0}+E_R/T_0$ there. Heat $Q$ positive into the system changes its energy by $\Delta E_R=-Q$, so $\Delta S_R=-Q/T_0$.

[A2] Ideal pressure store: at fixed external pressure $p_0$, its stored energy changes by $p_0\Delta V$ when the system volume changes by $\Delta V$; the only system work is $W_{\mathrm{on}}=-p_0\Delta V$. The store's entropy is constant. At fixed volume this store is absent. No other work coordinate or matter transfer is admitted.

[A3] The system and bath, with the pressure store when present, form an isolated compound with fixed total energy. In the fixed-volume case $\Delta U+\Delta E_R=0$; in the fixed-pressure case $\Delta U+\Delta E_R+p_0\Delta V=0$. These are explicit ideal-environment constraints; they do not follow from units.

[F1] [[post-td-first-law-energy]]: For admitted closed core-process records, $\Delta U=Q+W_{\mathrm{on}}$ with heat positive into the system and work positive on it, under fixed composition and zero excluded-energy endpoint changes.

[F2] [[post-td-macroscopic-second-law]]: For the admitted isolated compound with its named auxiliaries and equilibrium endpoints, $\Delta S_{\mathrm{tot}}\ge0$.

[F3] [[post-td-entropy-maximum]]: Stable equilibrium is an attained global maximum of the sum of constituent entropies on the explicitly declared feasible set; uniqueness is not assumed.

[F4] [[def-td-legendre-potentials]]: The local Helmholtz and Gibbs potentials are $F=U-TS$ and $G=U-TS+pV$ on their valid natural-variable charts.

[F5] [[def-td-si-quantities]]: $U$, $Q$, and work transfers are in joules, $T$ in kelvins, $S$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, $p$ in pascals, and $V$ in $\mathrm{m^3}$, with $\mathrm{Pa\,m^3=J}$.
sections.Proof:
1.1 In the fixed-volume case, the first-law balance [F1] has $W_{\mathrm{on}}=0$ by [A2], so $\Delta U=Q$. The bath relation [A1] gives $\Delta S_{\mathrm{tot}}=\Delta S-Q/T_0$. By [F2], $\Delta S_{\mathrm{tot}}\ge0$, and therefore $\Delta F_{T_0}=Q-T_0\Delta S=-T_0\Delta S_{\mathrm{tot}}\le0$. [given, A1, A2, F1, F2, F5, algebra]

1.2 In the fixed-pressure case, [A2] and [F1] give $\Delta U=Q-p_0\Delta V$, while [A1] gives $\Delta S_{\mathrm{tot}}=\Delta S-Q/T_0$. Hence $\Delta G_{T_0,p_0}=\Delta U+p_0\Delta V-T_0\Delta S=Q-T_0\Delta S=-T_0\Delta S_{\mathrm{tot}}\le0$. [given, A1, A2, F1, F2, F5, algebra]

1.3 For fixed volume, [A1] and [A3] express total entropy on the feasible set as $S_{\mathrm{tot}}=\mathrm{constant}-F_{T_0}/T_0$. Since $T_0>0$, maximizing total entropy is equivalent to minimizing $F_{T_0}$; on the natural-variable chart the function is the Helmholtz potential by [F4]. [A1, A3, F3, F4, algebra]

2.1 For fixed pressure, [A1]–[A3] express total entropy as $S_{\mathrm{tot}}=\mathrm{constant}-G_{T_0,p_0}/T_0$. Again $T_0>0$, so every attained global entropy maximizer on that feasible set is a global minimizer of $G_{T_0,p_0}$; on the natural-variable chart it is the Gibbs potential by [F4]. Neither equivalence implies uniqueness or attainment beyond [F3]. [A1, A2, A3, F3, F4, algebra] ∎
sections.Remarks: The assumptions define ideal reservoirs, not measured reservoirs. A finite bath generally has varying temperature and does not satisfy [A1] exactly. The result does not cover an open flowing control volume or other generalized work coordinates.

fm.title: Stable-tempered free-cube grand pressure
fm.physical_scope: Positive-temperature grand-canonical positional preparations in cubic free-wall boxes for stable even Borel pair potentials with the explicitly stated decreasing integrable tail.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics (author-hosted Cambridge lecture notes)
Konstantin K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Part SM: Statistical Mechanics (2024 author-hosted lecture notes)

sections.Statement:
Assume AC. Let $d\geq2$, $\varphi$ be stable with the regular integrable tail of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]], and assume its dimensionless representative $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$ is Borel measurable, as required by the current mathematical supplier. Take $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$, $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$, and $\widehat\beta=E_0\beta>0$. For cubes $\Lambda_L=[-L/2,L/2)^d$, let $\Xi_L(z,\beta)$ be the free-wall grand partition function specified by [[post-td-equilibrium-ensemble-sampling]]. Then the positional grand pressure
$$p_L(z,T)=\frac{k_BT}{\ell_0^d|\Lambda_L|}\log\Xi_L(z,\beta)$$
has a finite limit as $L\to\infty$. In the dimensionless reference-volume convention of [[thm-tdmath-canonical-grand-duality]], let $P(\alpha,\widehat\beta)=\lim_{L\to\infty}|\Lambda_L|^{-1}\log\Xi_L(e^\alpha,\widehat\beta)$, where the supplier uses numerical energies in units of $E_0$. Then $p=(k_BT/\ell_0^d)P(\log z,\widehat\beta)$. This is a conditional model deduction, not a measurement or an assertion that every real gas realizes the preparation.
sections.Facts & Assumptions:
[F1] [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]]: stability gives $H_N\geq-BN$, and the tail has a nonnegative decreasing envelope $\psi$ with $\int_R^\infty r^{d-1}\psi(r)\,dr<\infty$. The mathematical supplier uses numerical energy; $\widehat H=H/E_0$ and $\widehat\beta=E_0\beta$ preserve $\beta H=\widehat\beta\widehat H$.

[A1] [[post-td-equilibrium-ensemble-sampling]]: the finite-volume grand law uses $\Xi_\Lambda(z,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}z^NZ_{\Lambda,N}$ with $Z_{\Lambda,N}=\int e^{-\beta H_N}\,d\mu_{\Lambda,N}$.

[L1] [[thm-tdmath-canonical-grand-duality]]: the current carrier's statement defines the dimensionless grand rate from the free-cube activity sum, gives its limit under the stable regular tail hypotheses at positive numerical $\widehat\beta$, and states both Legendre--Fenchel identities for the specified closed effective-domain extension. The physical-to-numerical energy conversion is $\widehat\beta=E_0\beta$. The item and draft proof text are present, and its scoped batch-18 proof-contract entry passes; no Step 1 decision is recorded, so the conclusion remains conditional.
sections.Proof:
**Given:** AC, the stable regularly tempered Borel pair model, the adopted finite-volume positional grand preparation, and the current draft free-cube supplier statement in [L1]. No kinetic partition factor or empirical premise is used.

1.1 By [A1], the physical positional partition sum is $\Xi_L(z,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}z^NZ_{\Lambda_L,N}$. Set $\alpha=\log z$; then $z^N=e^{\alpha N}$. Translate the centered cube by $L/2$ in each coordinate to $[0,L)^d$; this preserves Lebesgue measure and every pair displacement, so the positional partition is exactly the free-cube sum of [L1]. The dimensionless energy conversion in [F1] matches its numerical $\widehat\beta$. [given, F1, A1, L1, algebra]

2.1 The conditional conclusion of [L1] gives a finite limit $P(\log z,\widehat\beta)$ for $|\Lambda_L|^{-1}\log\Xi_L$. Multiplying by $k_BT/\ell_0^d$, which is independent of $L$, converts the dimensionless reference-volume rate to pressure per physical volume. [given, F1, L1, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

Assume AC. Let $d\geq2$, $\varphi$ be stable with the regular integrable tail of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]], and assume its dimensionless representative $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$ is Borel measurable, as required by the current mathematical supplier. fm.physical_scope: A scope and hypothesis ledger for the preceding finite, countable, measurable, lattice, regular-shell and discrete-quantum branches; it supplies no additional ensemble-equivalence, ergodicity, thermalization, or empirical claim.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete lecture notes, §§1.2–1.3 (printed pp. 2–27)
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §§4.2–4.6 (printed pp. 192–217)

sections.Remarks:
The finite canonical, maximum-entropy, independent-factorization and finite-bath claims concern the exact finite state spaces and shell-weight assumptions stated in their items. Countable and measurable derivative identities require their local summable or integrable moment envelopes; a lower energy bound alone does not normalize the partition function. The lattice bulk-pressure and concentration claims apply only to the bounded finite-range lattice model and, for concentration, a differentiability point of the limiting log-partition density. The page-level continuum-pressure prerequisite is a distinct interaction model; no stable-tempered continuum limit is inferred from the lattice theorem.

The classical shell result applies only to a nonempty compact regular level with the coarea normalization and a globally defined invertible flow on the stated band. It does not imply ergodicity or equality of long-time averages with the shell law. The quantum trace identities require a semibounded self-adjoint generator, a positive finite Gibbs trace and the stated moment envelope; discrete dephasing is a trace-norm Cesaro limit with degenerate eigenspaces retained, not pointwise relaxation or a Gibbs limit.

Boltzmann microstate entropy, finite Gibbs entropy, von Neumann entropy and the macroscopic entropy function are distinct objects until a model supplies an explicit identification. The statistical value $-k_{\mathrm B}T\log Z$ is not silently identified with a macroscopic Helmholtz or grand potential. Canonical and microcanonical sampling are adopted preparation assumptions. None of the finite probability identities, continuum or lattice pressure limits, shell-invariance results or quantum trace calculations reports an experiment or establishes that nature follows the model.

fm.title: Additive extensive representation of compound comparison

references.title: Lieb and Yngvason, The Physics and Mathematics of the Second Law of Thermodynamics, Theorem 2.2
Campión et al., A Survey on the Mathematical Foundations of Axiomatic Entropy, §§2–5

sections.Statement:
Let $X$ be nonempty and suppose its finite-support compounds carry the comparison structure of [[def-tdmath-comparison-and-stability]] over the complete ordered field $\mathbb R$. If there are $x_0,x_1\in X$ with $x_0\preceq x_1$ and not $x_1\preceq x_0$, define $S(x):=\sup L_x$ using [[lem-tdmath-reference-supremum-bounds]]. Then $S:X\to\mathbb R$ is normalized by $S(x_0)=0$, $S(x_1)=1$, and for all equal-mass compounds $A=\sum_i a_i e_{x_i}$ and $B=\sum_j b_j e_{y_j}$,

$$A\preceq B\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\sum_i a_iS(x_i)\le\sum_j b_jS(y_j).$$

Thus $S$ is an additive extensive representation on finite compounds. If no strict pair exists, CH instead makes every equal-mass pair of compounds equivalent, and any constant state function gives a (degenerate) additive representation. No concavity, continuity, or physical law follows without additional hypotheses.
sections.Facts & Assumptions:
[A1] [[def-tdmath-comparison-and-stability]]: equal-mass compounds satisfy the preorder, consistency, scaling, stability and comparison hypotheses; the state set is nonempty.

[F1] [[def-tdmath-signed-comparison]] and [[lem-tdmath-spectator-cancellation]]: signed comparisons are translation-invariant and additive, and agree with ordinary comparison for nonnegative compounds.

[F2] [[lem-tdmath-reference-supremum-bounds]]: in the strict-reference case, each $S(x)=\sup L_x$ is finite and $x\sim_sR_{S(x)}$.

[F3] [[lem-tdmath-reference-order]]: $R_\lambda\preceq_sR_\mu$ iff $\lambda\le\mu$ for the chosen strict reference pair.

[F4] [[def-tdmath-tagged-scalable-compound]] and [[lem-tdmath-compound-mass-well-defined]]: each state denotes its unit-mass point compound $e_x$; every compound is the finite sum of its strictly positive support coefficients, or the empty sum. Nonnegative scaling is pointwise, $0C=0$, and a nonnegative compound has zero mass exactly when it is empty.
sections.Proof:
**Given:** [A1] and [F1]–[F4].

1.1 In the strict-reference case, [F3] gives $R_\lambda\preceq_s e_{x_0}$ exactly for $\lambda\le0$, and $R_\lambda\preceq_s e_{x_1}$ exactly for $\lambda\le1$. Their suprema are therefore $S(x_0)=0$ and $S(x_1)=1$. [F2, F3]

1.2 Let $C=\sum_i a_i e_{x_i}$ have mass $M$ and set $q_C:=\sum_i a_iS(x_i)$. Discard any zero terms in this presentation using [F4]. If the support is empty, $C=0$, $M=q_C=0$ and $C_R=0$, so signed reflexivity gives the claimed equivalence. Otherwise each remaining coefficient is strictly positive. For each remaining constituent, [F2] gives $e_{x_i}\sim_sR_{S(x_i)}$; positive scaling and finite repeated use of composition combine these into $C\sim_s C_R$, where $C_R:=\sum_i a_iR_{S(x_i)}=(M-q_C)e_{x_0}+q_Ce_{x_1}$. This calculation is valid for signed coefficients because the signed relation is additive and translation-invariant by [F1]. [A1, F1, F2, F4, algebra]

2.1 Apply step 1.2 to both $A$ and $B$, and write $q_A,q_B$ for the resulting scalar sums. Since $A\sim_sA_R$ and $B\sim_sB_R$, transitivity gives $A\preceq B$ exactly when $A_R\preceq_sB_R$. Their masses agree, and $B_R-A_R=(q_B-q_A)(e_{x_1}-e_{x_0})$; [F3] therefore gives $A_R\preceq_sB_R$ exactly when $q_A\le q_B$. This proves the representation formula. [A1, F1, F3, step 1.2]

3.1 In the no-strict-pair case, take any $x,y\in X$. By [F4] their unit compounds have equal mass one, so CH gives one of $x\preceq y$ or $y\preceq x$; if exactly one held it would be a strict pair, so both hold. Fix $r\in X$. Let $C$ have mass $M$. If $M=0$, [F4] gives $C=0$, and reflexivity handles this empty compound without applying the positive-scaling axiom at zero. If $M>0$, use the canonical finite decomposition over the support from [F4]; every coefficient there is positive. Scale each constituent equivalence $e_x\sim e_r$ by its positive coefficient and compose the finitely many comparisons to obtain $C\sim M e_r$. Thus equal-mass $A,B$ are both empty when their common mass is zero, and otherwise each is equivalent to the same $M e_r$; hence they are equivalent in both cases. For a constant $S(x)=c$, both compound values equal $cM$, including zero for empty compounds, so the representation equivalence holds. [A1, F1, F4, algebra] ∎

fm.title: Calibration of an arbitrary family of simple-system entropies

references.title: Lieb and Yngvason, The Physics and Mathematics of the Second Law of Thermodynamics, Theorem 2.5 and §IV.B.2, pp. 27–29, 56–59
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, Chapters 2 and 4, complete 607-page edition

sections.Statement:
Let $I$ be a nonempty set of primitive simple-system labels containing a distinguished meter label $m$. Assume every finite separated product is explicitly represented by its finitely many tagged elementary factors; positive scaling and finite product are the only identifications. Suppose the join-closed family satisfies the hypotheses of [[thm-tdmath-conditional-contact-calibrator]], and fix a strict meter pair $z_0\prec\prec z_1$ in $\Gamma_m$. Assume the Axiom of Choice. Then one can choose, for every $i\in I$, an additive constant and positive scale for its same-type entropy so that

$$S\big((t_1i_1,x_1),\ldots,(t_ni_n,x_n)\big)=\sum_{\ell=1}^n t_\ell S_{i_\ell}(x_\ell)$$

is additive, extensive, and characterizes every same-composition comparison on every finite separated product. No conclusion is asserted for transitions that change composition.
sections.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** The explicit finite-factor family, common contact branch, strict meter pair, and Axiom of Choice.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: every family of nonempty sets admits a choice function; it selects the reference states, entropy representatives, and calibrator data used below.

[F1] [[thm-tdmath-conditional-contact-calibrator]]: for each pair of simple types in the join-closed family, strict calibrator endpoints exist and their reversible pair relation identifies the two reference increments in signed comparison.

[F2] [[thm-tdmath-additive-entropy-representation]]: once a type and its scaled products have CH, a finite real additive extensive entropy represents their equal-mass comparisons.

[F3] [[def-tdmath-forward-signed-comparison]] and [[lem-tdmath-forward-spectator-cancellation]]: signed comparison is translation-invariant and additive, agrees with ordinary comparison on nonnegative equal-mass maps, and permits common-spectator cancellation.
sections.Proof:
**Given:** [A1], [F1]–[F3].

1.1 Use the positive type normalization in [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]] whenever invoking [F2]; state entropies evaluate represented maps $\mathsf{J}(x)$, and their unit-label entropy density is $S_i(x)/w_{\Gamma_i}$. Apply [F2] to the meter type and choose its entropy $S_m$ so $S_m(z_0)=0$ and $S_m(z_1)=1$. Set the meter reference to $r_m=z_0$, and use [A1] to choose a reference state $r_i$ and one same-type entropy representative for every $i\ne m$. For each $i\ne m$, use [F1] to choose calibrator states $a_i,b_i\in\Gamma_i$ and $c_i,d_i\in\Gamma_m$ such that $a_i\prec\prec b_i$, $c_i\prec\prec d_i$, and $(a_i,d_i)\sim(b_i,c_i)$; also choose $r_i\in\Gamma_i$. For the meter label set $a_m=c_m=z_0$ and $b_m=d_m=z_1$; the two pairs $(z_0,z_1)$ and $(z_1,z_0)$ are the same two-copy meter compound up to permutation. Write $S_i^0$ for the selected entropy representative, with $S_m^0=S_m$, and put $\Delta_i=S_i^0(b_i)-S_i^0(a_i)>0$ and $\mu_i=S_m(d_i)-S_m(c_i)>0$. Define $S_i(x):=\frac{\mu_i}{\Delta_i}\bigl(S_i^0(x)-S_i^0(r_i)\bigr)$. Then $S_i(r_i)=0$ and $S_i(b_i)-S_i(a_i)=\mu_i$, matching the meter entropy increment across the chosen calibrator endpoints. For $i=m$, $\Delta_m=\mu_m=1$, so this agrees with the fixed meter normalization. [A1, F1, F2, choose]

2.1 For a finite separated compound $A$ with factors $(t_\ell i_\ell,x_\ell)$, define $S(A):=\sum_\ell t_\ell S_{i_\ell}(x_\ell)$. The sum is finite and invariant under reordering; concatenating compounds adds the sums, and scaling every amount by $t>0$ multiplies it by $t$. The explicit-factor convention in the Statement therefore makes $S$ well-defined, additive, and extensive. [A1, step 1.1, construct]

3.1 Fix a composition with amounts $M_i$ for finitely many labels and let $A,B$ be two states of that same composition. For a state $x$ of type $i$, put
$s_i(x):=\frac{S_i(x)-S_i(a_i)}{\mu_i}.$
The same-type entropy representation and the CH for type $i$ show
$\mathsf{J}(x)\sim_s(1-s_i(x))\mathsf{J}(a_i)+s_i(x)\mathsf{J}(b_i).$
Indeed, the signed difference has total coefficient zero and $S_i$-value zero, so its positive and negative parts have equal mass and entropy and therefore compare both ways by [F2]. The calibrator relation gives
$(\mathsf{J}(b_i)-\mathsf{J}(a_i))\sim_s(\mathsf{J}(d_i)-\mathsf{J}(c_i))$
by taking the signed difference of $(a_i,d_i)\sim(b_i,c_i)$ and canceling common terms with [F3]. Add and scale these identities over the finitely many factors of $A$. With
$q_i(A):=\sum_{\ell:\,i_\ell=i}t_\ell s_i(x_\ell),$
the resulting signed map is
$A\sim_s \sum_i M_i \mathsf{J}(a_i)+\sum_i q_i(A)(\mathsf{J}(d_i)-\mathsf{J}(c_i)),$
where the sums range over the finite support of the composition. The same holds for $B$. Since they have the same composition, the reference base cancels, and $B-A$ is signed-equivalent to the finite meter map
$D:=\sum_i\bigl(q_i(B)-q_i(A)\bigr)(\mathsf{J}(d_i)-\mathsf{J}(c_i)).$
Extend the meter entropy linearly to raw finite signed coefficient maps using density $S_m(z)/w_{\Gamma_m}$ at a meter raw tag $(\Gamma_m,z)$; in particular its value on $\mathsf{J}(z)$ is $S_m(z)$. Then
$S_m(D)=\sum_i\bigl(q_i(B)-q_i(A)\bigr)\mu_i=S(B)-S(A).$
The positive and negative parts of $D$ have equal mass. If $S(A)\le S(B)$, the same-type entropy representation [F2] for finite meter products gives $D^-\prec D^+$, hence $D$ compares in the forward signed direction. Translation, addition, and ordinary-order compatibility [F3] transfer this to $A\prec B$. Conversely, if $A\prec B$, the same signed equivalences and translation in [F3] give $D^-\prec D^+$. The meter representation in [F2] then forces $S_m(D)=S(B)-S(A)\ge0$. Reversing the entropy inequality gives the reverse comparison. Thus $S$ characterizes every same-composition comparison. Each particular comparison uses only finitely many labels; no infinite sum or uncountable product occurs. [A1, F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 The meter normalization fixes the multiplicative unit. Changing the chosen reference state for type $i$ changes only its additive constant; on a finite compound these constants contribute amount-weighted conserved-type offsets. This proves the stated freedom and completes the construction. [A1, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra] ∎
sections.Remarks: AC is used only for simultaneous reference-state, entropy-representative, and calibrator choices over the arbitrary label set $I$. Cross-composition monotonicity requires the additional cost and offset hypotheses developed later.

references.title: H.-O. Georgii, Large deviations and the equivalence of ensembles for Gibbsian particle systems with superstable interaction
references.locator: Theorems 2 and 4, printed pp.175–178 / PDF pp.5–8, variational pressure and ensemble equivalence; the exact fixed-density extension is supplied by the local canonical proof.

references.title: D. Dereudre, Introduction to the theory of Gibbs point processes
references.locator: Section 2.6, PDF pp.24–26, finite-range Gibbs variational principle; the present tail class and endpoint conventions are proved locally.

sections.Statement:
Let $F_\beta$ be the finite concave canonical rate on the interior attainable-density interval from [[thm-tdmath-canonical-interior-density-limit]]. Extend it by $F_\beta(0)=0$, by its interior upper-semicontinuous limit at any finite upper endpoint of its effective domain, and by $-\infty$ outside the closed effective domain; retain the value $-\infty$ if the endpoint limit is $-\infty$. For $\alpha\in\mathbb R$, define
$$P(\alpha,\beta)=\lim_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log\Xi_L(e^\alpha,\beta),$$
whose existence is [[thm-tdmath-decreasing-integrable-tail-free-cube-pressure]]. Then
$$P(\alpha,\beta)=\sup_{\rho\geq0}\bigl(F_\beta(\rho)+\alpha\rho\bigr),\qquad F_\beta(\rho)=\inf_{\alpha\in\mathbb R}\bigl(P(\alpha,\beta)-\alpha\rho\bigr)$$
for every $\rho$ in the closed effective domain of $F_\beta$. These are thermodynamic limits of positional partition functions. They do not assert local-observable equivalence, a finite-volume endpoint realization, or a thin energy-shell limit.
sections.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** A stable regular pair potential, $\beta>0$, its free-cube canonical partition functions, and the exact entropy/rate conventions above.

[F1] [[thm-tdmath-canonical-interior-density-limit]]: for each interior attainable $\rho>0$ and every sequence $N_L/L^d\to\rho$, $L^{-d}\log Z(L,N_L;\beta)\to F_\beta(\rho)$; the proof supplies the slab-packing inequality and sparse low-density lower bound.

[F2] [[thm-tdmath-decreasing-integrable-tail-free-cube-pressure]]: stability bounds the grand tail exponentially and the free-cube grand-pressure limit exists for every positive activity.

[F3] [[thm-tdmath-finite-dimensional-biconjugation]]: a proper closed convex function on finite-dimensional Euclidean space equals its biconjugate under the stated extended-real conventions.

[A1] Stability supplies a finite $B\geq0$ with $U_N\geq-BN$ ([[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]).
sections.Proof:
**Given:** The hypotheses and suppliers in Facts & Assumptions.

1.1 Fix an interior attainable density $\rho>0$ and a sequence $N_L/L^d\to\rho$. The grand sum contains the nonnegative term $e^{\alpha N_L}Z(L,N_L;\beta)$, so $\liminf_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log\Xi_L(e^\alpha,\beta)\geq F_\beta(\rho)+\alpha\rho$ by [F1]. Taking the supremum over interior densities gives the lower bound. The vacuum term $Z(L,0)=1$ gives the value $0$ at density zero. Endpoint values are limits from the interior by their definition, so they do not enlarge the supremum. [F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 Put $q=e^{\alpha+\beta B}$. For each $N\geq0$, stability and the box-volume formula give $e^{\alpha N}Z(L,N;\beta)\leq(qL^d)^N/N!$. Choose $K>eq+1$. **Given:** Stability with constant $B$, a regular even pair potential, fixed $\beta>0$, and the free-cube canonical convention in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]].

[F1] Stability gives $U_N\geq-BN$ for every finite configuration; regularity gives an integrable decreasing two-sided tail envelope ([[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]).

[F2] For every sufficiently large gap $g$, the lattice-shell interaction tail is bounded by [[lem-tdmath-integrable-tail-diagonal-gap]], with a diagonal choice $g(\ell)/\ell\to0$ and vanishing cross-energy density.

[F3] The Lebesgue box and product-measure suppliers give volume $L^{dN}$ for the $N$-fold cube and permit factorization over disjoint cores ([[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]], [[thm-sigma-finite-product-measure-exists-is-rectangular-and-is-unique]], [[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]).

[F4] The factorial and logarithm suppliers give the integral bounds $\int_1^m\log x\,dx\leq\log(m!)\leq\int_1^{m+1}\log x\,dx$ and $\log(1+u)\leq u$ for $u>-1$ ([[def-factorial-and-falling-factorial]], [[thm-natural-logarithm-laws]]).
sections.Proof:
**Given:** The hypotheses and suppliers in Facts & Assumptions.

1.1 Stability and [F3] give $Z(L,N;\beta)\leq e^{\beta BN}L^{dN}/N!$. If $N/L^d\to\rho>0$, the factorial integral bounds [F4] imply $$ \limsup L^{-d}\log Z(L,N;\beta)\leq \rho(1+\beta B-\log\rho), $$ so $b(\rho)$ and $F(\rho)$ are bounded above on every compact positive-density interval. The vacuum term gives $b(0)=0$: $Z(L,0)=1$ is a lower bound, and the same stability estimate with $N/L^d\to0$ gives a nonpositive upper limit. [F1, F3, F4, algebra]

1.2 The effective domain of $F$ has nonempty interior. Fix a core cube of side $s>0$ and a gap $g>R_0$; place one particle in each selected core of a lattice of spacing $s+g$ inside a large box. The absolute interaction from any one occupied core to all others is bounded by $C\sum_{m\geq1}m^{d-1}\psi(mg)<\infty$ by [F1]–[F2]. Restricting each particle to a subcube of volume $v_0>0$ therefore gives $Z(L,N;\beta)\geq v_0^N e^{-C_0N}$ for every density strictly below $(s+g)^{-d}$, after omitting unused lattice cells. Thus $F$ is finite on a nonempty interval of positive densities; by its definition as a finite-mixture envelope it is concave. [F1, F2, F3, algebra, construct]

2.1 Fix a finite list of core preparations $(s_i,n_i)$ with $0<Z(s_i,n_i;\beta)<\infty$. For each $i$, choose a gap $g_i=g(s_i)$ from [F2] along a sequence $s_i\to\infty$ so that $g_i/s_i\to0$ and the positive interaction between distinct cores in the same lattice packing, divided by core volume, tends to zero. Set tile side $a_i=s_i+g_i$ and effective density $r_i=n_i/a_i^d$. If $M_i$ such tiles carry exactly $n_i$ particles in their central $s_i$-cubes, the same shell count as in the proof of [[thm-tdmath-decreasing-integrable-tail-free-cube-pressure]] gives cross-energy penalty per occupied volume at most $C (n_i/s_i^d)^2(s_i/g_i)^d\eta(g_i)$, which tends to zero by [F2]. Exact factorization over disjoint core cubes follows because assigning the labeled coordinates to their cores contributes $N!/\prod_i(n_i!)^{M_i}$, cancelling the global $N!$. [F2, F3, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 For any finite convex combination in the definition of $F(\rho)$, choose core preparations with densities tending to its $\rho_i$ and rates tending to $b(\rho_i)$. If their effective densities do not strictly bracket the target $\rho$, add arbitrarily small weights at one attainable density below and one above $\rho$; such densities exist because $\rho$ is interior. Their mixture coefficients can then be perturbed by quantities tending to zero so the effective mean is exactly $\rho$. Place the fixed core types in finitely many macroscopic slabs with these volume fractions, inserting fixed empty layers wider than $R_0$ between slabs. For fixed core sizes and gaps, the distinct-slab cross energy divided by total volume tends to zero: for interaction distances at most $R$, only $O(RL^{d-1})$ particles lie in the interface strips, while the remaining contribution is bounded by a constant times $L^d\sum_{|j|_\infty>R}\Psi_j$; take $L\to\infty$ and then $R\to\infty$. [F1, F2, step 2.1, construct]

4.1 First reserve an outer layer of fixed width $W$ and adjust slab fractions in the remaining volume to match the target density; the strict bracketing in step 3.1 absorbs the reserved layer's $O(WL^{d-1})$ volume without assuming its one-particle capacity replaces a bulk density. Rounding the finitely many core counts then changes particle number by at most $C_1L^{d-1}$ with $C_1$ depending on the fixed preparations, not on $W$, because only boundary tiles are incomplete. Choose $W$ large enough to contain at least $C_1L^{d-1}$ small cells separated from each other and every core by more than $R_0$. Put each missing particle in one such cell. Its interaction with the fixed preparations is bounded by the same summable tail, so the correction changes log weight by only $O(L^{d-1})$. This constructs exactly $N_L$ particles for every sequence $N_L/L^d\to\rho$, and gives $$ \liminf_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log Z(L,N_L;\beta)\geq\sum_i\theta_i\frac{\log Z(s_i,n_i;\beta)-\mathrm{cross}_i}{a_i^d}, $$ where $\mathrm{cross}_i/a_i^d\to0$ by step 2.1. Taking preparations approaching the selected convex combination and then the supremum gives $\liminf\geq F(\rho)$. [F1, F2, F3, step 2.1, step 3.1, construct]

5.1 By the definition of $b$, every sequence with density tending $\rho$ has limsup rate at most $b(\rho)\leq F(\rho)$. Together with step 4.1 this proves the asserted limit. A finite concave function on an open interval is continuous: fix $a<\rho<b$ in the interval; the chord slopes from $a$ and $b$ bound the difference quotients on a smaller interval around $\rho$, yielding a finite local Lipschitz bound. This establishes finiteness and continuity of $F$ on its effective interior while leaving excluded endpoints undecided. [F4, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 4.1, algebra] ∎

sections.Statement: Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+1}$, $n\ge1$, be open and let $\omega=\sum_{i=1}^n a_i dx_i+b dz$ be a $C^2$ one-form with $\omega_q\ne0$ near $q_0\in U$. sections.Proof:
**Given:** Translate $q_0$ to $(0,z_0)$. Restrict all fields and flows to a sufficiently small coordinate neighborhood of $q_0$.

1.1 Since $\omega_{q_0}\ne0$, one coordinate coefficient is nonzero at $q_0$; relabel that coordinate as $z$ and shrink the neighborhood so $b\ne0$. Put $c_i:=-a_i/b$ and $X_i:=\partial_{x_i}+c_i\partial_z$. Then $X_i\in C^2$, $\omega(X_i)=a_i+bc_i=0$, and the $X_i$ are a basis of $\ker\omega$ because their first $n$ components form the standard basis. [given, F1, construct]

1.2 Define $[X,Y]:=DY\,X-DX\,Y$. Coordinate expansion of the displayed formula for $d\omega$ gives $d\omega(X,Y)=X[\omega(Y)]-Y[\omega(X)]-\omega([X,Y])$. Thus for horizontal fields $d\omega(X_i,X_j)=-\omega([X_i,X_j])$. Also $[X_i,X_j]$ has zero $x$-components, hence is vertical. Evaluating the three-form on $(\partial_z,X_i,X_j)$ gives $(\omega\wedge d\omega)(\partial_z,X_i,X_j)=b\,d\omega(X_i,X_j)$. Under (i), $d\omega(X_i,X_j)=0$; then $\omega([X_i,X_j])=0$, and a vertical vector $v\partial_z$ has $\omega(v\partial_z)=vb$, so $[X_i,X_j]=0$. [F1, algebra]

2.1 By [F2]–[F3] and step 1.2, the fields $X_i$ have commuting local $C^2$ flows $\phi_i^t$. Define $\Phi(x,\eta):=\phi_n^{x_n}\circ\cdots\circ\phi_1^{x_1}(0,\eta)$ for $(x,\eta)$ near $(0,z_0)$. Each $X_i$ changes only $x_i$, at rate one, so the first $n$ coordinates of $\Phi(x,\eta)$ are exactly $x$. Commutation and the transported-field identity in [F3] give $\partial_{x_i}\Phi=X_i(\Phi)$. 3.1 Let $N=n+1$. On an open product neighborhood of $(u_0,y_0)=((0,z_0),(0,z_0))$ where $\Phi$ is defined, set $H(u,y):=\Phi(u)-y$. [step 2.1, step 3.1, F3, algebra]

5.1 Conversely, if (ii) holds, [F4] gives $\omega\wedge d\omega=0$ on that neighborhood, proving (i). [F4] ∎

fm.title: Finite-family calibration by a common meter

references.title: Lieb and Yngvason, The Physics and Mathematics of the Second Law of Thermodynamics, §II.E

sections.Statement:
Let $I$ be a finite nonempty set of system types, $X_i$ a nonempty state set with chosen reference $r_i\in X_i$ for each $i\in I$, and $M$ a common meter state set with $z_0,z_1\in M$. Assume for every $i$ that the product state set $X_i\times M$ satisfies the hypotheses of [[thm-tdmath-additive-entropy-representation]], with strict reference pair $(r_i,z_0)\prec\prec(r_i,z_1)$. Let $S_i$ be its normalized representation and put $\sigma_i(x):=S_i(x,z_0)$. In that product comparison, the unit product-state point mass satisfies $e_{(x,z_0)}\sim_s(1-\sigma_i(x))e_{(r_i,z_0)}+\sigma_i(x)e_{(r_i,z_1)}$, by [[lem-tdmath-reference-supremum-bounds]]. These product-state point masses are distinct from the shared state-and-meter compounds defined next.

Assume in addition a **common-meter compatibility interface**. Let $\mathcal Y$ contain disjoint families of raw state tags $a_{i,x}$, raw type-reference tags $\rho_i$, and two distinct raw meter tags $\zeta_0,\zeta_1$. Using the unit point masses on these tags, write $e_{r_i}:=e_{\rho_i}$ and $e_{z_j}:=e_{\zeta_j}$, and define $u_{i,x}:=e_{a_{i,x}}+e_{z_0}$. Thus $u_{i,x}$ is an explicit mass-two state-and-fixed-meter compound; it is not a unit tag. Compounds over $\mathcal Y$ use the finite-support convention of [[def-tdmath-tagged-scalable-compound]], and their signed comparison is the one in [[def-tdmath-signed-comparison]]. Require the exact substitution

$$u_{i,x}\sim_s e_{r_i}+(1-\sigma_i(x))e_{z_0}+\sigma_i(x)e_{z_1}\qquad(i\in I,\ x\in X_i),$$

finite substitutions to compose, and the fixed reference sum $\sum_iT_ie_{r_i}$ to cancel when type totals agree. Both sides of this signed substitution have total coefficient two, even when $\sigma_i(x)$ lies outside $[0,1]$. Require the common meter point masses to satisfy $e_{z_0}\preceq e_{z_1}$ and not $e_{z_1}\preceq e_{z_0}$. These are hypotheses on the comparison algebra, not consequences of separate numerical meter readings.

For positive coefficients $t_{ik}$ on a finite collection of type-$i$ states $x_{ik}$, define $T_i:=\sum_k t_{ik}$ and $T:=\sum_iT_i$. Put $C_0:=\sum_{i,k}t_{ik}e_{a_{i,x_{ik}}}$ and $C:=\sum_{i,k}t_{ik}u_{i,x_{ik}}=C_0+T e_{z_0}$. Thus $C_0$ is the state compound of mass $T$ and $C$ is its fixed-meter encoding of mass $2T$. Empty collections give $T=0$ and $C_0=C=0$. Define

$$\Sigma(C):=\sum_{i\in I}\sum_k t_{ik}\sigma_i(x_{ik}).$$

For two such compounds $C,D$ with the same type-total vector $(T_i)_{i\in I}$, the common comparison satisfies $C\preceq D$ exactly when $\Sigma(C)\le\Sigma(D)$. Equivalently, the same order criterion holds for the state compounds $C_0,D_0$ after canceling their common $T e_{z_0}$. The index family is finite; no arbitrary-index choice or infinite decomposition is asserted.
sections.Facts & Assumptions:
[A1] The common-meter compatibility interface in the Statement: the exact signed substitution for every $u_{i,x}$ holds, finite substitutions compose, equal type totals give the same cancellable reference sum, and the common meter pair is strict.

[F1] [[thm-tdmath-additive-entropy-representation]] supplies the real normalized product representation, and [[lem-tdmath-reference-supremum-bounds]] supplies $e_{(x,z_0)}\sim_s(1-\sigma_i(x))e_{(r_i,z_0)}+\sigma_i(x)e_{(r_i,z_1)}$ in its unit product-state comparison. The separate mass-two shared substitution is exactly [A1], not an identification of different product and shared tags.

[F2] [[lem-tdmath-spectator-cancellation]]: finite signed substitutions are additive and common terms can be canceled. [[def-tdmath-signed-comparison]] and [[def-tdmath-comparison-and-stability]] also preserve signed comparison under positive scaling: multiplying the difference by a positive scalar multiplies both its positive and negative parts by that scalar, so the compound scaling axiom applies.

[F3] [[lem-tdmath-reference-order]]: for the common strict meter pair, comparison of equal-mass reference expressions is exactly comparison of their $z_1$ coefficients.
sections.Proof:
**Given:** [A1] and [F1]–[F3].

1.1 For each constituent $(i,x_{ik},z_0)$ of $C$, its mass-two shared compound $u_{i,x_{ik}}$ is equivalent by the exact substitution in [A1] to $e_{r_i}+(1-\sigma_i(x_{ik}))e_{z_0}+\sigma_i(x_{ik})e_{z_1}$. Each side has total coefficient two, so this signed substitution is defined. Scale by $t_{ik}>0$ and combine the finitely many comparisons using [A1] and [F2]. The resulting reference-system part is $\sum_iT_i e_{r_i}$, independent of the chosen states. The meter part has coefficients $T-\Sigma(C)$ on $e_{z_0}$ and $\Sigma(C)$ on $e_{z_1}$, where $T:=\sum_iT_i$. Hence $C$ is equivalent to that fixed reference-system compound plus $(T-\Sigma(C))e_{z_0}+\Sigma(C)e_{z_1}$, whose total coefficient is $T+T=2T$. If the collection is empty, both expressions are zero and the equivalence is reflexivity, requiring no order scaling at zero. [A1, F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 The same substitution for $D$ gives the same reference-system compound because its type totals are the same, and the same total meter mass $T$. Cancel the common reference-system terms by [A1] and [F2]. If $T>0$, the remaining meter expressions have total coefficient $T$; positive scaling by $1/T$ turns them into the unit reference maps $R_{\Sigma(C)/T}$ and $R_{\Sigma(D)/T}$. By [F3] these compare exactly when $\Sigma(C)/T\le\Sigma(D)/T$, which is equivalent to $\Sigma(C)\le\Sigma(D)$. Scaling back by $T>0$ proves the reverse comparison equivalence, so no unit-mass reference theorem is applied directly at mass $T$. Reversing the same equivalences proves the converse implication as well. Since $C=C_0+T e_{z_0}$ and $D=D_0+T e_{z_0}$, [F2] also gives $C\preceq D$ exactly when $C_0\preceq D_0$; for $T=0$ all these compounds are empty and the criterion is $0\le0$. [A1, F2, F3, step 1.1] ∎
sections.Remarks: The compatibility interface records the compositional assumption needed to move from separate product systems to one shared meter scale. Without it, independent representations need not share a multiplicative calibration. This theorem makes no statement for infinitely many types.
