sections.Statement:
Assume a stable regular pair potential with the genuine positive-core condition of [[lem-tdmath-superquadratic-positive-core]]: a nonincreasing $\chi(r)>0$ satisfies $\phi(x)\geq\chi(|x|_\infty)$ near zero and $\int_0^{r_0}\chi(r)r^{d-1}dr=\infty$. For fixed $z,\beta>0$, define the exterior class
$$\Omega(t)=\{\zeta:\sum_{i\in\Lambda_n\cap\mathbb Z^d}N_{C_i}(\zeta)^2\leq t(2n+1)^d\text{ for every }n\}.$$
Then the free-wall grand pressure in $\Lambda_n=[-n-\tfrac12,n+\tfrac12)^d$, with the exterior pair energy against any $\zeta\in\Omega(t)$, converges to the free-cube pressure uniformly in $\zeta$. This statement is conditional on the genuine positive core; it does not infer that condition from superstability alone.
sections.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** The positive divergent core, regular far tail, fixed $z,\beta>0$, and a fixed finite tempering constant $t$.

[F1] [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]: the far pair interaction is bounded in absolute value by a decreasing integrable envelope.

[F2] [[lem-tdmath-integrable-tail-diagonal-gap]]: separated-cell tail sums tend to zero with gap.

[F3] [[lem-tdmath-superquadratic-positive-core]]: there is a superquadratic cell penalty $h(N)$ and $H\geq\sum_i h(N_i)-bN$.

[F4] [[thm-tdmath-decreasing-integrable-tail-free-cube-pressure]]: all perturbed free-cube grand pressures at positive activity and inverse temperature exist and are finite.

[F5] [[thm-holder-inequality-for-integrals]]: Hölder’s inequality gives convexity of finite-volume log partition functions in inverse temperature and log activity.

[L1] Ruelle's tempered-boundary estimates apply to superstable, lower-regular interactions with the stated square-count exterior class; the full source proof and exact hypotheses were read. The near/far estimate used below is written explicitly in the proof.
sections.Proof:
**Given:** The hypotheses and suppliers in Facts & Assumptions.

1.1 Write $T_n=\sum_{i\subset\Lambda_n}N_i^2$ and $V_n=|\Lambda_n|$. From [F3], $T_n$ is controlled by $H_n+bN_n$ and the superquadratic penalty dominates $N_i^2$ for large cell counts. For exterior cells at distance at least $k$, the lattice tail gives an energy lower error at most $\delta_k(T_n+c_tV_n)$, where $\delta_k\to0$. For the finitely many near exterior cells, use $mN\leq g(N)+g^*(m)$ with $g(N)=N\sqrt{h(N)}$. Since $g(N)/N^2\to\infty$, its Legendre transform satisfies $g^*(m)/m^2\to0$: for each $\epsilon>0$, $g(N)\geq N^2/(4\epsilon)-C_\epsilon$, so $g^*(m)\leq\epsilon m^2+C_\epsilon$. The exterior square-count bound then makes the near-cell contribution at most $\epsilon T_n+\epsilon V_n+O(n^{d-1})$, uniformly over $\zeta\in\Omega(t)$. [F1, F2, F3, L1, algebra]

2.1 Combining near and far estimates, for each $\epsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large $n$, the cross energy obeys $W(\omega,\zeta\setminus\Lambda_n)\geq-\epsilon T_n-\epsilon V_n$, uniformly in $\zeta$. Use $T_n\leq A_\epsilon(H_n+bN_n)+C_\epsilon V_n$ from [F3], and absorb the resulting linear-in-$N_n$ term into activity. This gives
$$\Xi_{n,\zeta}(\beta,z)\leq e^{c\epsilon V_n}\Xi_{n,\mathrm{free}}(\beta(1-c\epsilon),ze^{c\epsilon}),$$
for a fixed constant $c$ depending only on the coercivity constants. [F3, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 For the lower bound, restrict interior particles to a smaller cube with an empty corridor of width $k$. All exterior pairs are then in the far tail, and the same shell estimate bounds the absolute cross energy by $\epsilon T_{n-k}+\epsilon V_n$. The cell penalty absorbs the count term and yields
$$\Xi_{n,\zeta}(\beta,z)\geq e^{-c\epsilon V_n}\Xi_{n-k,\mathrm{free}}(\beta(1+c\epsilon),ze^{-c\epsilon})$$
uniformly over $\zeta$. The removed corridor volume fraction vanishes for fixed $k$. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Divide steps 2.1–2.2 by $V_n$ and take $n\to\infty$; [F4] supplies the perturbed cube pressure limits. These limits are finite convex functions of $(\beta,\log z)$, by Hölder’s inequality [F5], since finite-volume log partition functions are convex and pointwise limits preserve convexity. A finite convex function on an open parameter rectangle is continuous, by bounding coordinate secant slopes on a smaller rectangle. Let $\epsilon\downarrow0$ in both bounds. The upper and lower limits coincide with the free-cube pressure, uniformly over the entire exterior class. [F4, F5, step 2.1, step 2.2, algebra] ∎

sections.Statement:
Assume superstability and regularity, let $(\Omega_k)$ be van Hove, and let $N_k/|\Omega_k|\to\rho$ for an interior attainable density $\rho>0$. For the free-wall exact-$N_k$ positional partition with $1/N_k!$ normalization,
$$|\Omega_k|^{-1}\log Z(\Omega_k,N_k;\beta)\longrightarrow F_\beta(\rho),$$
the free-cube canonical rate of [[thm-tdmath-canonical-interior-density-limit]]. Superstability is used for the arbitrary-shape pressure upper bound; no stability-only upper theorem is asserted.
sections.Facts & Assumptions:
**Given:** The stated interaction, van Hove sequence, $\beta>0$, and interior density.

[F1] [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]: stability bounds canonical weights and the tail envelope is summable.

[F2] [[def-tdmath-van-hove-sequence]]: fixed-width geometric boundary layers have negligible volume.

[F3] [[thm-tdmath-canonical-interior-density-limit]]: free-cube exact-$N$ rates converge to finite concave $F_\beta$ on the attainable interior.

[F4] [[thm-tdmath-canonical-grand-duality]]: $F_\beta(\rho)=\inf_\alpha(P(\alpha,\beta)-\alpha\rho)$.

[F5] [[thm-tdmath-superstable-van-hove-pressure]]: the free grand pressure on $\Omega_k$ converges to the cube pressure.

[F6] [[lem-tdmath-integrable-tail-diagonal-gap]]: separated core lattice interactions have a vanishing diagonal gap bound.
sections.Proof:
**Given:** The assumptions and suppliers in Facts & Assumptions.

1.1 For any $\alpha\in\mathbb R$, $e^{\alpha N_k}Z(\Omega_k,N_k)\leq\Xi_{\Omega_k}(e^\alpha,\beta)$. Divide by volume, use [F5], and take the infimum over $\alpha$. The duality [F4] gives $\limsup |\Omega_k|^{-1}\log Z(\Omega_k,N_k)\leq F_\beta(\rho)$. [F4, F5, algebra]

1.2 Choose $\delta>0$ so $\rho-\delta,\rho+\delta$ lie in the attainable interior. For large core side $\ell$, choose integers $n_-,n_+$ with $n_\pm/\ell^d\to\rho\pm\delta$. Put a central $\ell$-cube inside each $(\ell+g)$-cell, with $g=g(\ell)$ from [F6]. The effective densities $n_\pm/(\ell+g)^d$ still bracket $\rho$ when $\ell$ is large. [F2, F3, F6, choose]

2.1 At fixed $\ell,g$, pack every complete $(\ell+g)$-cell contained in $\Omega_k$. Its count $M_k$ satisfies $M_k/|\Omega_k|\to(\ell+g)^{-d}$ by [F2]. ## Statement

$$|\Omega_k|^{-1}\log Z(\Omega_k,N_k;\beta)\longrightarrow F_\beta(\rho),$$
the free-cube canonical rate of [[thm-tdmath-canonical-interior-density-limit]]. Superstability is used for the arbitrary-shape pressure upper bound; no stability-only upper theorem is asserted.
